title: Genetic variability in biomass partitioning and surface residue carbon-nitrogen ratios in soybean
abstract: The drive to increase seed yield in soybean [Glycine max (L.) Merr.] has traditionally overshadowed the exploration of biomass partitioning and the compositional characteristics of plant residue traits such as leaves, petioles, stems, and pods. The exploration of biomass partitioning and the compositional characteristics of plant residue traits in soybean provide insights into plant nutrient allocation strategies that can be utilized to increase crop productivity and improve management practices for maximizing yields and sustainability. Recognizing this gap, our study aimed to investigate the variability in these traits across 32 genetically diverse soybean genotypes cultivated over 2 years in central Iowa. Through detailed collection and analysis of vegetative parts at critical growth stages (R1, R4, and R8), we assessed both biomass traits and their chemical compositional characteristics, focusing on soybean residue traits to enhance soil health and their importance in soybean cropping systems. We present broad sense heritability estimates for accumulated (R8) organ biomass (0.61–0.87) and residue carbon nitrogen composition (0.74) in soybeans. The large variation and high heritability suggest breeding strategies to optimize variety development via biomass and residue traits. Utilizing the Agriculture Production Systems sIMulator, we conducted a sensitivity analysis to evaluate the impact of soybean residue quality on soil nutrient cycling and its effects on the subsequent

title: Traffic Flow Characteristics in Work Zone and Non-Work Zone Environment and Its Impact on Road Crashes at the Segment Level
abstract: This study investigates relationships between congestion and travel time performance metrics and crashes on road segments. The study focuses on work zone routes in Iowa, utilizing 2021 commercially-available probe vehicle data and crash data. Travel time performance metrics were derived from the probe vehicle data, and crash counts were obtained from the crash data. Additional variables included road characteristics (traffic volume, road type, segment length) and a categorical variable for the presence of a work zone. A mixed effect linear regression model was employed to identify relationships between road segment crash counts and the selected performance metrics. This was accomplished for two sets of models that include congestion performance measures at different defining threshold values, along with travel time performance measures. The study results indicate that the congestion indicators, certain travel time performance measures, and traffic counts were statistically significant and positively correlated with crash counts. Indicator variables for rural interstate locations and non-active work zones have a stronger influence on crash count than those for municipal interstate locations and active work zones. These findings can inform decision-makers on work zone safety strategies and crash mitigation planning, especially in high traffic volume areas prone to congestion and queues.

title: A study of variation in bread based on the process variables real time and oven position
abstract: The properties of commercial bakery products vary due to random variance and special cause variance as described by Shewhart (1931). Descriptive tools have not been available, or have not been consistently utilized in the industry to objectively describe bread products. A need exists for objective measures of bread qualities which can be used for Statistical Process Control (SPC) to reduce special cause variability in the product and thereby increase quality. This study examined examples of a sweet white pan bread product made at a wholesale production facility of a major U.S baking company. Nine objective measures were used to describe the product: loaf height, loaf volume, moisture content, pH, TTA, crust color, compressibility, cell fineness, and cell elongation. The specific purposes of this study were to: (1) Determine if there were significant differences in the quality of bread baked on four consecutive days of a production week, as measured by nine parameters; (2) Determine if there were significant differences in quality due to oven placement, left or right, as measured by nine parameters; and (3) Determine if there were significant levels of interaction between production day and oven location (left or right side) of bread as measured by nine parameters.

title: Development of physically based curve models for use in a force feedback virtual environment
abstract: The problem being addressed is to enhance CAD packages by simplifying the way that the user manipulates the virtual object. The CAD packages will be enhanced by associating dynamic characteristics with the virtual object. The problem of associating dynamic characteristics with a virtual object for use in a real-time simulation has just begun to be explored by using finite element analysis (FEA). However, providing the capability for arbitrary free-form deformation will require the use of B-splines because of irregular shapes of the virtual object. While the use ofB-splines is common in CAD packages, associating dynamic characteristics with this representation has not been fully investigated.

title: Multivariate structure and concurrent validity of the 1994 Strong Interest Inventory
abstract:
Reviewed three areas within the field of vocational interest measurement. The first two areas, focusing on the history of both the field and of the Strong Interest Inventory, emphasize the tradition and innovation in vocational interest measurement. The value of the Strong Interest Inventory in predicting vocational behavior is the concluding focus. Book chapters, authored by three prominent figures in the modem history of the Strong Interest Inventory, were consulted. Overall, the early empirical tradition in vocational interest measurement created a sound foundation for the prediction of vocational behavior, as well as later innovation and theory building. 

Studied the relative contributions of the content scales to the predictive structure and concurrent validity of the 1994 Strong Interest Inventory. Criterion groups, representing 50 occupations, contained the 18,951 employed women and men in the General Reference Sample (Strong Interest Inventory Applications and Technical Guide, Harmon, Hansen, Borgen, & Hammer, 1994). Univariate and multivariate discriminant function analysis methods were used to compare the capacity of the Personal Style Scales, General Occupational Themes, and Basic Interest Scales to predict occupational group membership. Statistical indices (i.e., effect sizes) were provided to indicate the overall differentiation between occupational groups for each of the 35 scales. A predicted inverse relationship between the predictive power of each of the 3 s

title: An ethnography of a U.S. congressional office
abstract: Most congressional offices operate as open systems, constantly adapting to changes in their external environments. They resemble adhocracies much more so than their federal agency counterparts even though they still have a strong tie to bureaucratic structure. It is my contention in this study that federal bureaucratic agency organizations have a ''long row to hoe'' before they reach the status of point of origin structures because only then will congressional offices be able to deal more adequately with the constituency-service function of their organizations. I am not advocating that an adhocracy structure would be most desirable for congressional offices. It might, however, be much more adequate for handling expected uncertainties partially caused by external environmental factors including federal agency actions. I am advocating that federal government organizations--political offices as well as federal regulatory offices--must pay more attention to their environments by becoming more flexible so that bureaucratic barriers may be broken down for the purpose of responding more effectively to human needs.

title: Perceptions of reality at destination resort sites
abstract: The purpose of this study is to provide a conceptual framework for design professionals in an application-oriented process to decipher and interpret the various degrees of perceived reality that can be observed at destination resort sites. This framework will assist in the planning and design processes used to make informed decisions when developing new resort properties and to measure how physical design decisions can be perceived by the user.

title: Divining the father: A cenotaph for Alberti
abstract: This project does not explore the assertion that 'God is a woman'. It does however begin to look at the problems that are generated by the father, a divine and god-like father, specifically for men. It is also the problem of the father-god in architecture. Whitford's book suggests that woman has not yet arrived7 and that there is a "self-division" of both of man and woman. This project is intended to explore something of the relationship and the inhabitance of what remains a male-dominated discourse in a way that operates and does not allow men to see their "wholeness" whether illusory or not as being unproblematic for themselves as well as others.

title: Application of Artificial Neural Networks to Predict Solonchaks Index Derived from Fuzzy Logic: A Case Study in North Algeria
abstract: Soil salinization, particularly under irrigation in the arid regions of North Africa, represents a major constraint to sustainable agricultural development. This study investigates the Chott El Hodna region in Algeria, a Ramsar-classified wetland severely affected by salinization. Two representative soil profiles (P1 and P2) were initially characterized, revealing chemical properties dominated by calcium-chloride and calcium-sulfate types. Based on these findings, 26 additional profiles with moderate levels of gypsum, limestone, and soluble salts were analyzed. The limited number of profiles reflects the environmental homogeneity of the area, allowing the study site to be considered a pilot zone. Fuzzy logic was employed to classify soils, identify intergrade soils, and determine their degree of membership to Solonchaks within the Calcisol class, addressing the lack of precision in conventional classifications. Results indicate that 50% of soils are Solonchaks, 46.15% are Calcisols, and 3.85% are intergrades. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) revealed that soil solution chemistry is mainly governed by the dissolution of evaporite minerals (gypsum, halite, anhydrite) and the precipitation of carbonate phases (calcite, aragonite, dolomite). Statistical analyses using Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Multiple Linear Regression (MLR) demonstrated that ANN achieved superior predictive performance for the Solonchak index (Is), with R2 = 0.70 and RMSE = 0.17, compared with R2 =

title: Full Factorial Comparison of the Diagnostic Performance of Three Nucleic Acid Extraction Kits and Three PRRSV RT-qPCR Assays Using Swine Oral Fluids of Known Status
abstract: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome (PRRS) is one of the costliest diseases in swine production, causing >$1.2 billion USD in annual losses in the United States. Oral fluids are widely used for PRRS virus (PRRSV) surveillance, accounting for 42% of nearly 480,000 PRRSV RT-qPCR cases submitted to six Midwestern U.S. laboratories between 2020 and 2025. Despite this reliance, few studies have applied appropriate methodological approaches to compare the performance of commercial extraction and PRRSV RT-qPCR protocols for oral fluid specimens. In this study, we evaluated nine extraction-amplification protocols for PRRSV RNA detection, based on three commercial extraction kits and three commercial RT-qPCR assays. For each protocol, performance was evaluated using 314 oral fluid samples of known status (215 positive, 99 negative), collected under controlled conditions from 72 pigs assigned to five groups inoculated with contemporary PRRSV isolates and from one negative control group. The Cq values were normalized as efficiency standardized Cqs (ECqs) and then analyzed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. The mean amplification efficiencies ranged from 67 to 92%, repeatability from 0.98 to 0.99, and overall reproducibility was 0.91. The ROC AUCs ranged from 0.916 to 0.986, with significant pairwise differences (p < 0.05). At optimal ECq cutoffs, sensitivities ranged from 83 to 98.1% with 100% specificity. Normalization enabled objective protocol comparisons

title: Kinetic-based techno-economic and life cycle assessment of slaughterhouse waste co-digestion for renewable natural gas production
abstract:
There is a critical need for research into clean alternative energy sources to address future energy requirements. Renewable natural gas (RNG) can play a key role in sustainably meeting the projected increasing demand for natural gas. This study presents a techno-economic analysis (TEA) and life cycle assessment (LCA) of the anaerobic co-digestion of slaughterhouse waste (SW), domestic waste (DW), and bovine manure (BM). A kinetic model based on experimental data was developed and integrated into BioSTEAM, providing a robust evaluation of process performance and feasibility. The proposed process achieved higher biogas yields and produced biochar as a valuable co-product, contributing to a reduction in the minimum selling price (MSP) of RNG. The
plant is projected to generate approximately 172 GJ⋅year−1 RNG, with an estimated MSP of 2.1 $ kg−1 RNG. The global warming potential (GWP) was calculated at −4.73 kg CO2−eq kg−1 RNG, highlighting the environmental benefits of co-digestion and the carbon sequestration potential of biochar. Sensitivity analysis identified residence time and the inoculum-to-substrate ratio (ISR) as the main factors influencing MSP and emissions, respectively. This integrated framework, combining experimental kinetic data, process modeling, TEA, and LCA, demonstrates the technical, economic, and environmental feasibility of waste-based RNG production systems, offering insights into circular bioeconomy strategies for sustainable energy and carbon managemen

title: Predictive Modeling for Enhanced Truck Parking Information Systems Using Machine Learning
abstract: The growing demand for truck freight in the United States has intensified the shortage of truck parking, posing safety and operational challenges. While real-time Truck Parking Information and Management Systems (TPIMSs) offer current availability, predictive insights remain limited. This study develops hybrid machine learning and deep learning models to forecast truck parking utilization for both pretrip and en-route decision-making. A site-specific gradient boosting model achieved the best pretrip performance (average root mean square error [RMSE] = 0.154), while a long short–term memory–based truck parking site utilization prediction (TPSUP) model provided accurate en-route predictions (RMSE = 0.0429) with a one-hour horizon. To enhance usability, a “Popular Times” panel was designed to visualize predictions through intuitive, color-coded charts. These tools support safer and more efficient parking decisions, laying the groundwork for a more robust and predictive TPIMS.

title: Model-Free Inference for Characterizing Protein Mutations through a Coevolutionary Lens
abstract: Multiple sequence alignment (MSA) data play a crucial role in the study of protein mutations, with contact prediction being a notable application. Existing methods are often model-based or algorithmic and typically do not incorporate statistical inference to quantify the uncertainty of the prediction outcomes. To address this, we propose a novel framework that transforms the task of contact prediction into a statistical testing problem. Our approach is motivated by the partial correlation for continuous random variables. With one-hot encoding of MSA data, we are able to construct a partial correlation graph for multivariate categorical variables. In this framework, two connected nodes in the graph indicate that the corresponding positions on the protein form a contact. A new spectrum-based test statistic is introduced to test whether two positions are partially correlated. Moreover, the new framework enables the identification of amino acid combinations that contribute to the correlation within the identified contacts, an important but largely unexplored aspect of protein mutations. Numerical experiments demonstrate that our proposed method is valid in terms of controlling Type I errors and powerful in general. Real data applications on various protein families further validate the practical utility of our approach in coevolution and mutation analysis.

title: Impacts of Soil Health Practices on Hydrologic Processes
abstract: Soil health, defined as the continued capacity of soil to function as a vital living ecosystem, plays a critical role in agricultural productivity, water quality, and climate resilience. This paper synthesizes current research on the impacts of soil health practices—such as reduced tillage, cover cropping, and residue management—on hydrologic processes within agricultural and urban systems. These practices influence water infiltration, storage, and movement through the soil-water-atmosphere continuum, reducing runoff, erosion, and surface water contamination while potentially moderating flood risks. Enhanced soil organic matter (SOM) and aggregate stability improve water holding capacity and infiltration, contributing to drought resilience and crop productivity. However, effects on groundwater recharge remain uncertain due to limited long-term data. The paper also explores the interplay between soil health and climate change, highlighting how improved soil management can mitigate adverse hydrologic impacts of extreme weather events. Policy implications emphasize adaptive governance and integration of farmer-led and indigenous practices to scale soil health adoption. Overall, soil health practices offer significant potential to enhance ecosystem services, water quality, and societal resilience in the face of climate variability.

title: Projection and assessment of future droughts in Iowa: developing a machine learning model and an interactive application
abstract: Climate change has intensified the frequency and severity of droughts, significantly impacting water resources, agriculture, and ecosystems. Traditional drought indicators typically focus on recent conditions rather than future projections, and conventional forecasting methods often struggle to capture the complex, non-linear relationships between long-term climate variables and droughts. This project aims to fill this gap by developing a machine-learning model to project drought conditions in Iowa, specifically focusing on the U.S. Drought Monitor categories. The developed model, a Long Short-Term Memory neural network, was validated to assess its reliability and accuracy. With a Root Mean Squared Error of 0.19 and an R2 of 91%, the model achieved a high level of accuracy, making it effective in guiding conservation practices and enabling timely interventions. The model was trained on historical data from 2012 to 2019 and thoroughly evaluated using out-of-sample data from 2002 to 2011. It exhibited strong performance in the projection of drought conditions across Iowa’s Hydrologic Unit Code 08 watersheds. Drought conditions for the period 2030–2050 were projected using three general circulation models (GCMs): MPI-ESM1-2-HR, BCC-CSM2-MR, and CNRM-ESM2-1. These projections were conducted under two contrasting Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs): SSP1-2.6, representing a low-emissions sustainability scenario, and SSP5-8.5, reflecting a high-emissions, fossil–fuel–intensive tra

title: Water balance analysis in Iowa using satellite-based evapotranspiration, precipitation, and streamflow data
abstract: Understanding the water balance in intensively managed agricultural landscapes is critical for sustainable water resource management. This study utilizes publicly available satellite-based evapotranspiration, gridded precipitation, and in-situ streamflow data to conduct water balance analysis for Iowa from 2000 to 2023. The objectives of the study were to: 1) identify areas of groundwater-dependent evapotranspiration, 2) evaluate the Budyko framework for estimating annual runoff, and 3) quantify the impact of historical land cover change on watershed hydrology. Our analysis revealed that during dry years, annual evapotranspiration exceeded precipitation across nearly 36,260 km2 of cropland. Approximately, 20 % of this area is sustained by irrigation, and the remaining 30,000 km2 rely on natural subsidies like stored soil moisture, or shallow groundwater. For a selected watershed, we showed that the Budyko framework is a good proxy for observed annual runoff (R²=0.83). Finally, we quantified that the historical conversion from native prairie to corn and soybean cropland has increased average annual runoff by approximately 57 mm (23 %), a direct result of the lower evapotranspiration rates of annual row crops.

title: CySIDER: Cybersecurity Situational Intelligence Framework for DER Networks
abstract: The growing integration of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) within the smart grid has increased its exposure to significant cyber-physical threats. Intrusion and anomaly detection systems (IADS) are employed to enhance situational awareness, but they often generate large volumes of low-level alerts with limited context, thereby reducing their operational value for security analysts. Additionally, current cyber situational awareness tools lack the depth to support DER cybersecurity, limiting the Security Operation Center’s (SOC) ability to detect, interpret, and respond effectively. This paper presents CySIDER, a real-time Cyber Situational Intelligence framework designed to strengthen cybersecurity visibility in DER networks. CySIDER integrates edge-based machine learning anomaly detection with cloud-level alert correlation and knowledge-graph reasoning to transform raw alerts into coherent high-level incident representations. The framework supports standardized threat mapping through the MITRE ATT&CK model and contextual analytics for rapid, informed response. The framework is validated within an experimental testbed environment using DER-specific datasets, achieving low prediction latency (≈ 2 ms) and high alert confidence (≈ 96%), with high alert reduction and correlation rates. This framework is protocol-agnostic and IADS-platform independent, making it a scalable and practical solution to secure next-generation DER networks.

title: Roadmap on methods and software for electronic structure based simulations in chemistry and materials
abstract: This Roadmap article provides a succinct, comprehensive overview of the state of electronic structure (ES) methods and software for molecular and materials simulations. Seventeen distinct sections collect insights by 51 leading scientists in the field. Each contribution addresses the status of a particular area, as well as current challenges and anticipated future advances, with a particular eye towards software related aspects and providing key references for further reading. Foundational sections cover density functional theory and its implementation in real-world simulation frameworks, Green’s function based many-body perturbation theory, wave-function based and stochastic ES approaches, relativistic effects and semiempirical ES theory approaches. Subsequent sections cover nuclear quantum effects, real-time propagation of the ES, challenges for computational spectroscopy simulations, and exploration of complex potential energy surfaces. The final sections summarize practical aspects, including computational workflows for complex simulation tasks, the impact of current and future high-performance computing architectures, software engineering practices, education and training to maintain and broaden the community, as well as the status of and needs for ES based modeling from the vantage point of industry environments. Overall, the field of ES software and method development continues to unlock immense opportunities for future scientific discovery, based on the growing abilit

title: Prediction of stability constants of metal–ligand complexes by machine learning for the design of ligands with optimal metal ion selectivity
abstract: The new LOGKPREDICT program integrates HostDesigner molecular design software with the machine learning (ML) program Chemprop. By supplying HostDesigner with predicted log K values, LOGKPREDICT enhances the computer-aided molecular design process by ranking ligands directly by metal–ligand binding strength. Harnessing reliable experimental data from a historic National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) database and data from the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC), we train message passing neural net algorithms. The multi-metal NIST-based ML model has a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.629 ± 0.044 (R2 of 0.960 ± 0.006), while two versions of lanthanide-only IUPAC-based ML models have, respectively, RMSE of 0.764 ± 0.073 (R2 of 0.976 ± 0.005) and 0.757 ± 0.071 (R2 of 0.959 ± 0.007). For relative log K predictions on an out-of-sample set of six ligands, demonstrating metal ion selectivity, the RMSE value reaches a commendably low 0.25. We showcase the use of LOGKPREDICT in identifying ligands with high selectivity for lanthanides in aqueous solutions, a finding supported by recent experimental evidence. We also predict new ligands yet to be verified experimentally. Therefore, our ML models implemented through LOGKPREDICT and interfaced with the ligand design software HostDesigner pave the way for designing new ligands with predetermined selectivity for competing metal ions in an aqueous solution.

title: Big Data Analytics to Estimate Benefit Cost Ratios for FEMA Mitigation Projects
abstract: The FEMA Hazard Mitigation Assistance (HMA) program funds community projects is designed to reduce the impacts of natural disasters. But many project records lack benefit cost ratio (BCR) values, limiting efforts to assess project effectiveness. This study develops predictive models to estimate missing BCRs using other FEMA published project variables, including program area, region, state, status, project amount, and net value benefit. Multiple modeling strategies were evaluated, beginning with linear regression and machine learning models before moving onto Bayesian hierarchical models. Linear and machine learning models revealed weak relationships between BCR and the other project variables. Bayesian hierarchical models produced consistent results across model specifications, indicating no meaningful differences in how project variables relate to BCR. These findings suggest that BCR and net value benefit may be influenced by subjective assessments or human adjustments, a pattern supported by visual analysis of the empirical BCR distribution. Overall, the analysis indicates that existing project attributes provide limited predictive power for estimating BCR, and new methods will need to be used to find potential correlations for modelling.

title: Chemist: A Domain-Specific Language by Chemists for Chemists
abstract: Managing the complexity of quantum chemistry (QC) software is key to ensuring it remains accessible, maintainable, and reusable. Noticeably missing from the QC ecosystem are modules targeting bottleneck routines. Here we argue that this is likely due to the difficulty in defining interfaces for such modules. To that end, we introduce the open-source, publicly available Chemist library https://github.com/NWChemEx/Chemist. Chemist is a domain-specific language targeting the QC domain. Chemist has been developed focusing on performance and user-friendliness. Using Chemist, QC tasks are defined using familiar domain concepts such as molecules, wave functions, and operators. The domain objects are hierarchical to ensure a systematic encapsulation of information. Key features of Chemist include: extensibility, the ability to alias existing data, and the ability to succinctly define many common QC tasks. The usefulness of Chemist is demonstrated by discussing the interface of NWChemEx’s Fock build module and by showcasing a proof-of-concept self-consistent field algorithm containing uncertainty propagation.

title: A Platform Approach for Designing Sustainable Indole Thiosemicarbazone Corrosion Inhibitors with Enhanced Adsorption Properties
abstract: With an estimated global cost of $2.5 trillion per year, metal corrosion represents a major challenge across all industrial sectors. Numerous inorganic and organic corrosion inhibitors have been developed, but there are growing concerns about their toxicity and impact on the environment. Here, superior organic corrosion inhibitors based on indole-3-carboxaldehyde, a compound commonly found in the digestive system, and thiosemicarbazones, a safe class of ligands, were designed and studied for mild steel in pH 1 sulfuric acid solutions. Electroanalytical techniques and gravimetric tests revealed inhibition efficiencies as high as 98.9% at 30 °C. Models using Langmuir isotherms gave adsorption equilibrium constants Kads of 2 to 9 x 104 M-1 and corresponding Gibbs free energies of adsorption (ΔGads) as high as -41.44 kJ mol-1, indicating their chemisorption. SEM images confirmed the efficacy of these corrosion inhibitors, as surface features showed limited to no changes after tests. Surface analysis by XPS and LC-MS revealed inhibitor concentrations in the order of 0.7 to 1.8 μg cm-2 for the best compounds, further underlining their performance at low concentrations. Mapping of the surface by MALDI-MS further confirmed the homogeneous coating of the steel surface, with no visible fluctuations in concentrations. As all inhibitors shared the same indole thiosemicarbazone platform, unique structure-performance relationships were drawn from theoretical calculations. Notably, DFT and

title: NWChem: Past, present, and future
abstract: Specialized computational chemistry packages have permanently reshaped the landscape of chemical and materials science by providing tools to support and guide experimental efforts and for the prediction of atomistic and electronic properties. In this regard, electronic structure packages have played a special role by using first-principle-driven methodologies to model complex chemical and materials processes. Over the past few decades, the rapid development of computing technologies and the tremendous increase in computational power have offered a unique chance to study complex transformations using sophisticated and predictive many-body techniques that describe correlated behavior of electrons in molecular and condensed phase systems at different levels of theory. In enabling these simulations, novel parallel algorithms have been able to take advantage of computational resources to address the polynomial scaling of electronic structure methods. In this paper, we briefly review the NWChem computational chemistry suite, including its history, design principles, parallel tools, current capabilities, outreach, and outlook.

title: Feasibility Informed Advantage Weighted Regression for Persistent Safety in Offline Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Safe offline reinforcement learning aims to learn policies that maximize cumulative rewards while adhering to safety constraints, using only offline data for training. A key challenge is balancing safety and performance, particularly when the policy encounters out-of-distribution (OOD) states and actions, which can lead to safety violations or overly conservative behavior during deployment. To address these challenges, we introduce Feasibility Informed Advantage Weighted Actor-Critic (FAWAC), a method that prioritizes persistent safety in constrained Markov decision processes (CMDPs). FAWAC formulates policy optimization with feasibility conditions derived specifically for offline datasets, enabling safe policy updates in non-parametric policy space, followed by projection into parametric space for constrained actor training. By incorporating a cost-advantage term into Advantage Weighted Regression (AWR), FAWAC ensures that the safety constraints are respected while maximizing performance. Additionally, we propose a strategy to address a more challenging class of problems that involves tempting datasets where trajectories are predominantly high-rewarded but unsafe. Empirical evaluations on standard benchmarks demonstrate that FAWAC achieves strong results, effectively balancing safety and performance in learning policies from the static datasets.

title: "Characterizing, modelling, and simulation of the agricultural rubber track system "
abstract:
This dissertation presents a investigation into dynamic modeling, simulation, and experimental characterization of rubber track systems used in agricultural machinery. The primary objectives of this study are threefold: (1) to investigate and quantify the material properties of rubber track composites through carefully designed physical experiments, focusing on stiffness and damping characteristics; (2) to develop a two-dimensional multibody dynamic model of a continuous rubber track system based on first principles and calibrated using experimentally identified system parameters; and (3) to evaluate model through both qualitative and quantitative analyses of its dynamic responses, with sensitivity analysis performed to assess the influence of key parameters. 
The first objective of this study was to investigate and quantify the material properties of rubber track composites through carefully designed physical experiments. Tensile and bending tests were performed on fiber- and steel-reinforced track specimens using an Instron 3367 universal testing machine with custom-designed clamping fixtures to ensure secure gripping and controlled loading. The experimental design included multiple strain rates (5–500 mm/min) to capture potential viscoelastic rate effects, with each condition repeated to assess consistency. Data were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) to statistically separate fixed effects (displacement, strain rate, bending angle) from random effects (repl

title: Global optimization of mixed-integer nonlinear programs via decision diagrams
abstract:
Mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) provides a robust modeling framework for representing
real-world decision-making problems involving discrete and continuous variables under
nonlinear relationships. However, despite decades of progress in mixed-integer linear and convex
programming, global solution methods for general MINLPs remain limited in scalability and
scope, particularly when dealing with nonconvex, nonsmooth, or irregular problem structures that
challenge existing convexification techniques. This dissertation develops a graph-based global optimization
framework based on decision diagrams (DDs) that advances the state of the art in solving
complex MINLPs. The proposed approach departs from traditional algebraic formulations and
instead represents nonlinear constraints as structured graphs that capture variable dependencies
and enable the design of strong convex relaxations. The framework integrates DD-based reformulations,
linear outer approximations, and a spatial branch-and-bound algorithm with convergence
guarantees, providing the first general-purpose DD-based solution methodology for global MINLPs.
Building on this foundation, the second part of the dissertation extends the graphical framework
to statistical estimation problems with nonconvex regularization functions, such as the smoothly
clipped absolute deviation (SCAD) and minimax concave penalty (MCP). These models, widely
used for inducing sparsity and improving estimator properties, have historical

title: Benchmarking the Impact of Retrieval Augmented Generation on HPC Source Code
abstract:
High Performance Computing (HPC) systems are critical enablers of scientific discovery and industrial innovation. As global challenges such as climate change, biomedical research, and material science continue to demand increasingly complex simulations and analyses, the ability to efficiently develop optimized parallel code has become more important than ever. Frameworks like OpenMP provide a pathway for developers to implement parallelism in shared-memory systems, yet utilizing them effectively requires significant domain knowledge. These challenges are exacerbated by the growing complexity of computational hardware and the steep learning curve associated with HPC toolchains.
At the same time, the rapid evolution of Large Language Models (LLMs) has opened new frontiers in code generation, allowing developers to automate routine programming tasks. Despite their strengths, general-purpose LLMs are constrained by outdated training data and lack the nuanced understanding required for domains such as HPC.
As part of this project, we collaborated with Ph.D. students from the Janesari Lab to upgrade an exisiting benchmark framework that integrates Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) techniques into the code generation pipeline to address these limitations. By retrieving relevant and domain-specific context from external corpora like GitHub repositories and StackOverflow discussions, and encoding them using sophisticated embedding models such as GIST and CodeSearch, we enable LLMs

title: Design and Evaluation of a Tool for URL Phishing Detection
abstract: In this report, I describe the design and implementation of a system for phishing URL  detection which operates by checking different patterns in website addresses to find out if they are safe or malicious. Phishing is a major problem on the internet because attackers use fake websites  to trick people into giving away passwords, bank details, or other sensitive information. Since a phishing attempt often begins with a suspicious link, detecting it early can stop many attacks. The system I built looks at two kinds of features. First, it uses character-level patterns such as  symbols, repeated characters, and unusual strings. Second, it uses handcrafted features like the  length of the URL, number of digits, the use of “@” symbols, subdirectory depth, and whether  the domain is written as an IP address. These features help show the difference between phishing  links and normal websites.  The system was tested with several machine learning models, including Logistic Regression,  Support Vector Machines, Naive Bayes, Random Forest, and XGBoost. I used a dataset of  phishing and legitimate URLs, and measured performance using accuracy, precision, recall,  F1-score, and ROC-AUC. The results showed that Random Forest and XGBoost worked the best,  while Logistic Regression and SVM also gave strong results with less computation. Naive Bayes  performed more simply but still gave a useful baseline. One strength of this system is that it does  not need to download the full website conte

title: Insurance Risk Decision Engine: Automated Renter Eligibility Assessment & Dynamic Pricing System
abstract:
This report presents the design, implementation, and deployment of an Insurance Risk Decision Engine for Bonzah auto insurance. The system automates renter eligibility assessments and implements dynamic pricing strategies based on comprehensive risk analysis. The implementation follows a two-phase approach. Version 1 (V1) establishes core functionality with background check integration via Checkr API and implements a points-based conviction assessment system, achieving automated decision-making with complete regulatory explainability. Version 2 (V2) extends this foundation by incorporating sophisticated premium calculation models that consider age demographics, criminal conviction history, geographic location, vehicle classification, and rental duration.
The system processes insurance quote requests in real-time using AWS Lambda serverless architecture. Key innovations include a points-based conviction classification system covering 256 violation types with weighted scoring, automated background check integration, granular age-based risk factors for ages 17-100, state-based pricing with two rate tiers, and dynamic duration discounts for 1-30+ day rentals. The premium calculation model analyzes multiple risk factors simultaneously to generate fair, data-driven pricing.
Testing on 500 October 2025 rental transactions demonstrated the system's effectiveness. The conviction assessment correctly identified 84.6% of applicants as eligible and 15.4% as ineligible based on criminal h

title: TownGallery: Inspiring Creative Community
abstract: TownGallery is a smartphone application which encourages users to create hand-drawn artwork inspired by their real-world surroundings and then position these creations in Augmented Reality space for other users to see. The intent is to use AR as a means of allowing users to directly and artistically comment on physical public space. Through this technology, I hope to encourage more joyful and spontaneous creation of art, create new channels for artists and creative people to connect, and allow for people to, in some way, reclaim the public spaces of their communities.

title: Comparative Explainable AI for Loan Approval Predictions
abstract: This project develops and compares three machine learning models Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest to predict loan approval decisions with high accuracy. Using a dataset of 4,269 loan applications. The key contribution is integrating SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) to make model predictions interpretable for both regulators and applicants, addressing the critical need for transparency in lending decisions.

title: NeuroNav - Real-Time Hazard Detection for Blind Pedestrian
abstract:
Blind and visually impaired (BVI) pedestrians face heightened safety risks at street crossings due to the increasing prevalence of low-noise electric and hybrid vehicles, which diminish the reliability of auditory cues. Existing assistive technologies, including white canes, GPS-based tools, and obstacle detectors, do not provide real-time detection of moving vehicles, leaving a critical gap in urban mobility support. We present NeuroNav, a smartphone-based, multimodal hazard detection system that delivers real-time vehicle awareness through the integration of computer vision, spatial audio, haptic cues, and speech feedback.

Using contextual inquiry with BVI participants (n = 8), we identified key design requirements related to trust calibration, cognitive load, multimodal redundancy, and the need for confidence-aware alerts. We implemented a functional prototype using Unity, AR Foundation, and on-device inference to simulate real-time detection while ensuring accessibility alignment with WCAG 2.1. A usability study with BVI participants (n=6) demonstrated high comprehensibility of voice alerts (M=6.2/7), strong preference for customizable sensory settings (M=6.8/7), and consistent successful task performance. Participants expressed strong adoption intent (4/6), particularly for unfamiliar or acoustically complex environments.

Findings highlight the importance of integrating native screen reader support, refining haptic discrimination thresholds, and establishing alert-thro

title: The impact of AI on the emotional wellness of event planners: Exploring efficiency and emotional support tools
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes ingrained in the fabric of the event planning industry, its potential impact on the emotional wellness of planners remains underexplored. This qualitative study investigates how AI-based tools for automation and communication influence professional stress, resilience, and workplace satisfaction among event coordinators and managers. Guided by Conservation of Resources (COR) theory and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), semi-structured interviews were conducted with nine diverse event professionals across various roles and career stages. Thematic analysis revealed six major themes: Enhanced Efficiency & Task Management, Communication & Professionalism Aid, Stress and Burnout Mitigation, Motivation, Meaning, and Creativity, Barriers, Risks, and Frustrations, and Learning, Adoption, & Culture. Participants generally credited AI with reducing cognitive load and streamlining repetitive tasks, but also raised concerns about over-reliance, loss of creativity, and the “robotic” feel of some interactions. The study highlights the critical role of organizational culture, peer support, and tool usability in shaping whether AI acts as a buffer against burnout or a source of new stress. Practical implications and recommendations for future research are discussed, with an emphasis on fostering supportive environments that balance technological innovation with human-centered values in event planning.

title: LLM – Based Real Time Speech Reconstruction and Emergency Call Prioritization
abstract:
Emergency communication systems often suffer from disruptions due to packet loss, bandwidth limitations, and poor VoIP signal quality, making it difficult for dispatchers to assess the urgency of a situation. Additionally, victims in distress may struggle to convey critical information due to panic, speech disorders, or background noise, leading to incomplete or ambiguous communication. This paper proposes an LLM-based real-time speech reconstruction and emergency call prioritization system to address these challenges. The proposed system integrates real-time audio transcription with retrieval-augmented input conditioning using TF-IDF and FAISS indexing to retrieve relevant emergency transcripts, enhancing contextual understanding. Unlike traditional Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) models, this approach eliminates the need for fine-tuning, making it lightweight and efficient for real-time applications.
The reconstructed speech output is further classified using a GPT-based severity detection model, ensuring that critical emergencies receive immediate attention via Twilio and AssemblyAI APIs. Experimental evaluations demonstrate high Conceptual Precision and favorable BLEU and ROUGE scores, indicating strong alignment with real-world emergency scenarios. The results highlight the system’s potential to improve emergency response efficiency, optimize call triaging, and reduce communication delays in high-risk situations

title: SkillUp
abstract: This project presents a comprehensive user experience design for a job posting web application that connects freelancers with employers. Through detailed user journey mapping, we identified five critical phases in the employment lifecycle: Need, Search, Apply, Hire, and Work. The research reveals significant pain points in the current job posting ecosystem, particularly during the Search phase where users experience decision fatigue from overwhelming choices and difficulty filtering relevant opportunities. Our analysis shows emotional fluctuations throughout the user journey, with satisfaction dipping to 35% during search activities due to information overload and rising to 80% during the hiring phase when clear expectations are established.

title: Analyzing the Influence of Spatter Dynamics and Melt Pool Stability on Additive Manufacturing Performance Through Data analytics and Advanced Image Processing Techniques
abstract:
Additive manufacturing (AM) has transformed how industries design and produce high-precision
components, but maintaining consistent process stability remains a major challenge. This project
integrates programming, data analytics, and visualization to evaluate the in-situ behavior of
spatters and melt-pool stability in Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) systems. Using high-speed
imaging data from controlled experiments, a Python-based analytical pipeline was developed to
automatically detect, track, and analyze metallic spatter formation and melt-pool geometry. The
workflow combines image segmentation, feature extraction, and time-series analysis to quantify
parameters such as spatter count, ejection speed, ejection angle, and melt-pool length variation
over time.
The extracted features were then processed statistically to calculate a data-driven stability index,
which numerically represents the steadiness of the LPBF process. The framework leverages
Python libraries such as OpenCV, NumPy, Pandas, and Matplotlib for automated data handling,
computation, and visualization.
This study demonstrates how data-centric methodologies can enhance additive manufacturing by
converting experimental imaging data into structured, decision-ready insights. The integration of
programming, analytics, and visualization provides a scalable pathway toward smart
manufacturing systems that support process optimization, continuous monitoring, and quality
assurance in real time bridging the gap between ex

title: HospitalFlow: An Information System for Patient Scheduling and  Resource Management
abstract:
Hospitals handle hundreds of patient visits every day, and most of these visits depend on the 
proper scheduling of appointments, staff availability, and medical resources[1,7,12,21].When 
these activities are not well organized, hospitals face long waiting times, patient frustration, and 
slow service[3,13,23]. Many healthcare facilities still use outdated or manual systems such as 
phone calls, paper-based scheduling, or basic software that cannot keep up with real- time 
changes[12,17,25]. This leads to overlapping appointments, delays, miscommunication, and 
unnecessary stress for both patients and hospital staff[5,6,27]. From a Management Information 
Systems (MIS) point of view, these issues reduce overall efficiency, increase costs, and make it 
difficult for hospitals to operate smoothly[11,24]. This shows the need for a digital system that 
can manage patient flow, allocate resources properly, and help the hospital run more efficiently. 
This project introduces HospitalFlow, a digital information system designed to manage patient 
appointments, staff schedules, and resource allocation in hospitals [9,10,30]. The system 
includes features such as real-time appointment booking, automated reminders, digital queue 
management, bed and room allocation, lab test scheduling, and doctor availability tracking 
[25,10,18]. It helps patients by showing open time slots, estimated wait times, and appointment 
instructions [11,23]. For administrators, HospitalFlow offers dashboard

title: Breathe: An Exploration of Compulsive Technology Use and Technology-Based Solutions
abstract: The continued proliferation of technology in our daily lives has resulted in adverse consequences regarding our behavior and cognitive capabilities. Design patterns, social contracts, and other elements amount to habitual use that can cause lower mental health quality and feelings of guilt or discontent. This project approaches the issue from the framework of user-centered design, where the problem is ideated through the lens of User Experience Design and Research, understanding the pain points users have and what solutions could be employed to mitigate harms. Users were interviewed throughout the project from initial interviews identifying user sentiment to evaluating concepts to a final round of usability testing. Other design thinking strategies like competitive analysis and iterative design were also applied throughout to identify the best solutions in the space and what design features led to the intended outcome. The result was a product concept called Breathe, an app that intentionally adds friction when initiating an app of the user's choice. The project highlights the power of friction used as a deterrent toward behavior but also uses elements like user-imposed goals and customizable messages to further motivate the user toward correction. Results from the usability testing and development of the product identified a need for personalization when creating goals and messages to be sufficient enough for the individual. The project as a whole identified the key componen

title: Secure by Design: Why Organizations Must Prioritize Cybersecurity in Software and Infrastructure Development
abstract: Organizations continue to face significant cybersecurity risks as infrastructure and software systems evolve. Many times, security is treated as an afterthought, addressed only after vulnerabilities surface. The creative component investigates why embedding cybersecurity principles into software and infrastructure design from the beginning, commonly referred to as Secure by Design, is essential for reducing risks, lowering costs, and increasing organizational resilience. This project draws on peer-reviewed literature and industry reports published within the past 15 years to examine secure software development practices, system architecture, governance strategies, and their organizational impacts. The findings are categorized across key themes: cost-effectiveness, compliance and regulatory requirements, governance and leadership, human impact, and real-life examples. Overall, this creative component demonstrates how proactive security approaches, such as the National Institute of Standards and Technology Cybersecurity Framework (NIST CSF), mitigate risks more effectively than reactive strategies by bridging academic insights with practitioner frameworks and highlighting the economic, technical, and managerial advantages of Secure by Design.

title: A Comparative Study of Hive and Spark SQL for Batch Analytics Performance
abstract:
With the increasing amount of user interaction and transaction data generated by e-commerce platforms, organizations are relying more on data-driven decision-making for pricing, inventory planning, marketing optimization, and overall business strategy. Many of the most important measures of business performance, like Gross Merchandise Value (GMV), conversion rate, and repeat purchase rate, are derived through offline batch analysis workflows that need to process large datasets in a reliable and efficient way. Thus, designing a proper data architecture to enable these analytics tasks is critical to enabling insights to be delivered consistently and on a scale.
Despite the advancement of big-data processing frameworks, organizations have yet to determine the appropriate execution engine for analytical workloads on a large scale. Of all technologies in use today that are SQL-compatible, Hive SQL and Spark SQL are two of the most popular and commonly employed in batch analytics in modern data ecosystems. Historically, Hive SQL has executed processing with a MapReduce or Tez engine within a distributed framework, while Spark SQL executes analytical endeavors using in-memory computation with Catalyst optimizer that tends to provide a speedier execution time of analytical queries. Overall, while Spark SQL and Hive SQL generally present different latencies and performance profiles, the business implications of processing data with either Hive SQL or Spark SQL are context-dependent an

title: Exploring Prompt and Model Variability in Large Language Model Interpretations of Intrusion Detection Data
abstract:
Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) play a critical role in identifying and mitigating malicious activity in network traffic. While traditional machine learning approaches have advanced this field, they struggle to adapt to evolving threats. Recent progress in large language models (LLMs) presents new opportunities to enhance IDS by leveraging their contextual reasoning and generative capabilities. Despite this, there has been limited research on how different LLMs and prompting strategies can influence the accuracy in cybersecurity applications. 

This study investigates the application of four LLMs: Grok, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, which were tested on their ability to classify malicious and benign traffic using the CTU-13 dataset over four different prompts. These prompts vary in complexity. Evaluation metrics include accuracy, consistency, runtime, and readability of the outputs.  

The findings of this study indicate that simpler prompts yield more accurate classifications across all the LLMs. Gemini had the highest number of false positives but was the fastest model, while Grok was the most accurate but was the slowest model. Claude and ChatGPT had comparable, balanced performances. These results show that prompts have a significant impact on LLM performance.  

Overall, this study highlights both the promise and limitations of LLMs in network intrusion detection. While they are not yet viable as standalone IDS solutions, LLMs may serve as valuable assistive tools for a

title: AI-Driven Quality Control Database System for Manufacturing Setting
abstract:
In manufacturing, Quality Control (QC) data are often stored in static databases, leading to a
problem known as ”lost institutional memory”. When recurring issues happen, teams waste
valuable engineering hours re-diagnosing problems that have already been solved because the
context behind the original fix was lost.
To solve this, a prototype system was developed within Microsoft Excel. The system uses a
Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) macro to perform a ”file-based handshake” with an external
Python script. This script queries the Google Gemini API, providing it with a new QC finding
along with the complete historical context of all past findings related to that specific subassembly.
The system was tested using three distinct case studies: a hands-on process deviation, a
personnel-focused training gap, and an error caused by unclear design documentation. The results
show that the refined AI prompt successfully enabled the system to identify recurring patterns,
categorize the probable root cause (e.g., ”Process Deviation,” ”Documentation Error”), and
provide prioritized, actionable recommendations. The AI demonstrated its ability to differentiate
between a first-time fix and a recurring problem, suggesting a deeper inspection of the previous
solution.
This creative component demonstrates that a hybrid Excel-Python architecture is a practical
and accessible method for creating an intelligent feedback loop. The system successfully

title: From Dermoscopy to Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Survey on AI-Driven Skin Cancer Detection and Classification
abstract: Skin cancer is the most commonly diagnosed malignancy worldwide, and early detection is critical to improving patient survival rates. This survey offers a comprehensive overview of recent advances in skin cancer taxonomy and classification, as well as artificial intelligence (AI) approaches for automated diagnosis. We examine the hierarchical classification of skin lesions, ranging from benign conditions to malignant melanomas and keratinocyte carcinomas. The survey reviews state-of-the-art deep learning methods, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), vision transformers (ViTs), attention mechanisms, and ensemble learning techniques. We also discuss critical challenges, including data imbalance, limitations in dataset diversity, model interpretability, and clinical validation. Furthermore, we explore emerging areas including explainable AI (XAI), federated learning for privacy preservation, and multimodal fusion approaches. This survey aims to serve as a reference for researchers and practitioners working at the intersection of dermatology and artificial intelligence.

title: Insurance Risk Decision Engine: Automated Insurance Risk Assessment and Dynamic Pricing System for Rental Vehicle Coverage
abstract:
This report presents the design, implementation, and deployment of an Insurance Risk Decision Engine for Bonzah auto insurance. The system automates renter eligibility assessments and implements dynamic pricing strategies based on comprehensive risk analysis. The implementation follows a two-phase approach. Version 1 (V1) establishes core functionality with background check integration via Checkr API and implements a points-based conviction assessment system, achieving automated decision-making with complete regulatory explainability. Version 2 (V2) extends this foundation by incorporating sophisticated premium calculation models that consider age demographics, criminal conviction history, geographic location, vehicle classification, and rental duration.

The system processes insurance quote requests in real-time using AWS Lambda serverless architecture. Key innovations include a points-based conviction classification system covering 256 violation types with weighted scoring, automated background check integration, granular age-based risk factors for ages 17-100, state-based pricing with two rate tiers, and dynamic duration discounts for 1-30+ day rentals. The premium calculation model analyzes multiple risk factors simultaneously to generate fair, data-driven pricing.
Testing on 500 October 2025 rental transactions demonstrated the system’s effectiveness. The conviction assessment correctly identified 84.6% of applicants as eligible and 15.4% as ineligible based on criminal

title: Real-Steel: Perceptive Motion Retargeting for a Humanoid Boxer
abstract: This project presents Real-Steel, a real-time motion retargeting system that transforms human boxing motions into joint commands for the Unitree G1 humanoid robot. The system integrates computer vision through MediaPipe pose estimation, dual inverse kinematics solvers (analytical and optimization-based), and motion smoothing techniques to achieve robust robot control suitable for research and experimental applications.The core innovation lies in the dual-pipeline architecture that combines the speed of analytical geometric IK (3.86ms convergence) with the superior accuracy of Binary Real Particle Swarm Optimization (BRPSO) IK (79.7% error reduction). This enables runtime switching between speed-optimized and accuracy-optimized solutions based on application requirements. Experimental validation demonstrates the system’s effectiveness across four complexity scenarios, achieving 91.7% success rates for complex poses with 80.6% reduction in motion jitter compared to traditional methods. The complete system operates at 15-30 FPS end-to-end latency, making it suitable for real-time humanoid robot control applications.The project contributes a modular framework for human-robot motion retargeting, validated through testing and suitable for experimental deployment on the Unitree G1 platform. All components are integrated into an interactive system with visual feedback, runtime controls, and performance analytics.

title: Effect of different combinations of sites of action of pre-emergence herbicides on soybean emergence and early growth
abstract:
Herbicides are the backbone of weed control in field crops, including soybeans. Resistance to herbicides is increasing in the number of weed species, across various herbicidal chemicals, and across geographies, with resistant populations. Field scale weed control requires growers to apply herbicidal chemicals with multiple sites of action to assure that all important weed species are controlled including some with populations present resistant to one or more chemicals.
Recommended practice today for soybean growers is to apply both pre-emergence and post-emergence herbicides, each with multiple sites of action.  The tolerance of soybeans to pre-emergence herbicides to tank mixes formulated by growers to contain multiple sites of action is not well studied.
This study was of four different herbicidal chemicals (pendimethalin, saflufenacil, imazethapyr, pyroxasulfone) each having a different site of action.  The study design was a full factorial design of five replicate pots each with 7 seeds and was conducted on a growth table.  All herbicides were applied at twice the label maximum.  Growth conditions were designed to be highly uniform and closely approximating field conditions by using soil rather than potting medium, quantified PAR energy exposure and soil moisture maintained using continuous soil water status monitoring.
There were 13 responses derived from the timing of emergence, unifoliate stage and first trifoliate stage plus biomass and un-emerged seed autopsy.  Analy

title: The Effects of Tar spot (Phyllachora maydis) on Zea mays and Appropriate  Management Techniques
abstract:
Tar spot, caused by the fungal pathogen Phyllachora maydis, has emerged as one of the most destructive foliar diseases affecting corn (Zea mays) in North America since its first identification in the United States in 2015. This capstone project provides a comprehensive review of the disease’s biology, symptomology, epidemiology, and agronomic consequences, with an emphasis on actionable management strategies. Yield losses from tar spot can exceed 50 bushels per acre, largely due to accelerated senescence and stalk degradation, posing major challenges for harvest and profitability. The review explores the principles of the disease triangle, the environmental conditions conducive to tar spot development, and the interaction of tar spot with other common corn pathogens. A central focus is placed on integrated management practices, including fungicide efficacy and timing, hybrid selection, residue management, and the utility of decision-support tools. Based on extensive research, including multi-state fungicide trials and disease loss assessments, this work aims to provide farmers, agronomists, and extension specialists with a science-based, practical guide for identifying and mitigating tar spot.
The urgency of improved education, hybrid resistance development, and continued research is emphasized as critical to sustaining corn production in the face of this evolving threat.

title: A Theoretical Framework for Integrating MicroRNA Biomarker Data with Clinical   Information Systems in Cancer Research: Advancing Precision Medicine Through Health Informatics
abstract: Integration of miRNA biomarker data into Clinical Information Systems (CIS) is a significant advancement in realizing precision medicine in cancer therapy. Though the potential applications of miRNAs for diagnosis as well as prognosis have been established, miRNAs are currently used in a controlled manner in medicine because of technological, administrative, as well as regulatory, barriers (Calin & Croce, 2006; Lu et al., 2025). This paper proposes an effective and modular approach to safely and feasibly integrate miRNA data with CIS, utilizing global standards such as HL7 FHIR R4 and the OMOP Common Data Model (Health Level Seven International, 2024; Observational Health Data Sciences and Informatics [OHDSI], 2024; InterSystems, 2024; Wei et al., 2018). The paper employs a mixed methodology that involves systematic reviews, as well as scenario validation, to efficiently deal with challenges of data exchange, privacy, as well as support in clinical decisions. Application pathways, including automatic ETL processing for miRNA data, data transformation, as well as API integration via FHIR, also allow for easy application of this methodology. Four case validation studies are provided to demonstrate its viability in real-world settings. These include implementations of HL7’s FHIR genomic standard integrating into clinical workflows, Vanderbilt's PREDICT genomic program focusing on implementing genomic decision support into clinical practice, use of tumor boards for secure collabo

title: Neural Network Activation Manipulation for Automated Bug Fixing
abstract:
This research investigates the application of activation steering techniques to improve au-
tomatic program repair (APR) capabilities in large language models. Through systematic
manipulation of neural network activations at specific layers, we demonstrate that code
generation models can be guided to produce more correct and syntactically valid program
repairs.
The implemented system explores activation steering across multiple state-of-the-art code
generation models including Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, Qwen2.5-Coder-14B and CodeLlama-7B
[13, 14], evaluating performance on established benchmarks including HumanEval-Java [12]
and Defects4J [24]. Our approach utilizes contrastive pairs of correct and incorrect code
examples to extract steering vectors that encode the semantic difference between desirable
and undesirable program behaviors, following recent work on activation steering [23].
Results demonstrate significant improvements in code generation accuracy through strate-
gic application of steering vectors at middle-to-late network layers. On HumanEval-Java,
CodeLlama achieved the most substantial improvement, increasing from 35.62% to 56.25%
accuracy (20.63 percentage point improvement) using steering at layers 28–31 with strength
1.5. Qwen2.5-Coder-7B showed improvement from 58.13% to 70% (11.87 percentage point
improvement) with steering at layers 19–23, while the larger Qwen2.5-Coder-14B model im-
proved from 60.62% to 68.75% (8.13 percentage point improvement) at layers 43–47.

title: The Impact of Cybersecurity on Operations and Supply Chain Management
abstract:
The rapid digitalization of global operations and supply chains has significantly increased
organizational exposure to cyber threats. As firms adopt integrated platforms such as
ERP, WMS, TMS, cloud collaboration, and industrial control systems, they gain visibility
and efficiency but also inherit new cyber-physical vulnerabilities. Cybersecurity has
therefore become a core enabler of operational continuity, supply chain resilience, and
competitive performance rather than a purely technical concern.
This Creative Component synthesizes academic and practitioner literature to examine
how cybersecurity threats affect operations, production systems, logistics, and multi-tier
supply chain networks. Drawing from management information systems, operations and
supply chain management, cybersecurity, and IT governance, the study reviews the
evolving threat landscape, analyzes prominent incidents such as NotPetya, SolarWinds,
Colonial Pipeline, and JBS Foods, and explores their operational and supply chain
consequences.

The review further evaluates key risk management and resilience frameworks, including
the NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF), NIST SP 800-161 for Cyber Supply Chain
Risk Management (C-SCRM), ISO/IEC 27001, and Zero Trust Architecture. It highlights
the importance of integrating IT governance and business process management (BPM) to
embed “secure-by-design” principles into operational workflows and vendor
relationships. The findings underscore the need for holistic, cro

title: Mobile Application for AI SafeHand
abstract: The AI-SafeHand project aims at enhancing the safety of the firefighter by developing an AI-aided smart glove fitting and recommendation system based on hand anthropometric measurements. This creative component focuses on the design and development of the AISafeHand Mobile application, which serves as the user interface for collecting data and interacting. The application enables the fire fighters to sign up, capture a 2D image of their hand and securely send data for analysis through a backend API built using the Spring framework. The mobile application is built using React Native and Expo. The mobile application is built for both Android and iOS operating systems in order to maintain consistency in functionality and usability across devices. Core modules implemented are user registration, image capturing, and feedback collection interfaces, which set the stage for future integration with AI-driven glove suggestion capabilities. The app has been iteratively tested through both emulators and real devices to ensure performance, reliability, and usability. This work demonstrates the feasibility of using cross-platform mobile development and secure data pipelines to facilitate AI-based ergonomic studies and lays the groundwork for future deployment of customized glove recommendation systems for firefighters.

title: KidneyCare: Smart Health Management for Chronic Kidney Disease
abstract:
Long-term Kidney Dysfunction is a long-lasting health condition that needs continuous 
monitoring, timely medication, structured diet control, and regular communication with 
healthcare professionals [1,4,11]. Many patients struggle to manage these responsibilities due 
to the complexity of their treatment routines, frequent appointments, and the emotional stress 
of dealing with a chronic illness [1,16]. Caregivers and family members also face challenges in 
coordinating care, tracking symptoms, and staying updated on patient needs. These issues lead 
to missed appointments, poor medication adherence, inconsistent diet management, and delayed 
detection of worsening symptoms [10,11,22]. As a result, there is a critical need for an 
information system that simplifies kidney-care management while supporting both patients and 
caregivers. 
The KidneyCare project addresses this problem by proposing an integrated mobile health 
information system designed to support CKD patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers. The 
app centralizes key functions such as dialysis scheduling, automated medication reminders, AI 
based diet recommendations, symptom logging, fluid intake tracking, emergency alerts, and 
secure communication with medical teams [3,4,17]. The system also offers multilingual 
support, voice navigation, and accessibility features to support elderly users and individuals 
with low digital literacy [11,22]. By organizing critical health information into one platform,

title: Firewall Rule Optimization and Automation for Enhanced Network Security
abstract:
The exponential growth of networked systems has rendered traditional firewall rule management increasingly inadequate. Static configurations are ill-equipped to adapt to the dynamic nature of modern cyber threats, leading to inefficiencies, policy drift, and vulnerabilities. This research addresses the urgent need for a paradigm shift in firewall optimization by critically examining the current landscape of rule management methodologies, spanning algorithmic reordering, anomaly detection, high-level policy translation, and emerging applications of artificial intelligence.

Through an extensive meta-analysis of over thirty scholarly and industry sources, this study synthesizes advances across rule semantics, automated synthesis, and intelligent orchestration of access control policies. While isolated tools and frameworks demonstrate efficacy in targeted subdomains, they often fall short of delivering a cohesive, scalable solution for real-time, adaptive security governance.

To solve these problems, this project introduces a system that combines live traffic analysis, rule verification, and automatic rule adjustment. The system is modular and can work on different platforms, making it flexible for various network setups. It goes beyond traditional firewalls by creating an automated, efficient, and policy-based approach to managing firewall rules.

This project moves toward smarter and faster firewall optimization that can adapt to changing network conditions. It provides an im

title: Multi-Objective Planning for Autonomous Robots
abstract:
Autonomous robots often operate in environments where navigation involves multiple, potentially conflicting objectives. Traditional path planning methods, such as those used in the ROS Navigation2 (Nav2) stack, optimize a single additive cost function. However, many real-world problems require reasoning over hierarchically structured and non-comparable objectives—for example, prioritizing safety above efficiency, or law compliance above travel time. To address these limitations, this project implements a custom multi-objective path planning plugin for the Navigation2 framework, based on the theoretical framework presented in “Hierarchical Multiobjective Shortest Path Problems” by Slutsky et al. (2020).

The referenced paper introduces a graph-based algorithm that extends the classical shortest path problem to handle multiobjective cost structures represented as ordered combinations of algebraic cost monoids. This formulation allows for objectives that are not easily merged into a single additive cost, while maintaining computational efficiency through an iterative graph search procedure. Building upon this foundation, the project develops a custom Nav2 planner plugin that integrates this hierarchical multiobjective planning algorithm into both simulated and physical ROSBot platforms. The system enables autonomous robots to compute paths that respect objective hierarchies, adapt dynamically to environmental changes, and maintain optimal performance across competing goals.
