title: Methodological contributions to off-policy evaluation under the sample weighting framework and empirical financial analysis using semiparametric machine learning
abstract:
This dissertation investigates two interrelated research themes situated at the intersection of statistical learning and decision-making under uncertainty. The first theme emphasizes the application of machine learning methodologies to financial statistics, specifically targeting the robust modeling of conditional asset price distributions. Recognizing the limitations of traditional statistical models in capturing the skewness, heavy tails, and rare-event sensitivity inherent in financial markets, I propose a deep quantile regression-based forecasting approach. This methodology significantly improves tail-region predictions and enables the empirical analysis of option-implied risk premia through comparative analysis between predicted physical and risk-neutral densities. Additionally, I develop a novel financial flexibility index by integrating
structured econometric models with qualitative textual analysis of corporate disclosures using advanced large language models.
The second theme advances methodological frameworks in off-policy evaluation for reinforcement learning. Addressing challenges posed by data derived from historical policies, I refine the debiased calibration weighting approach to produce estimators exhibiting semiparametric efficiency and double robustness. This methodology is further generalized to sequential decision-making scenarios, providing multiply robust estimators applicable to dynamic policy evaluations.

title: Data assimilation using dynamically consistent inversion for model reactive flow problems
abstract:
The performance of various Monte Carlo-based data assimilation techniques for parameter estimation in reactive compressible flow models is investigated. Three primary approaches are evaluated: Ensemble Kalman Inversion (EKI), Ensemble-based Variational (EnVar), and Particle Filter methods. These gradient-free techniques are systematically assessed across multiple test cases of different complexity, including simple exponential models, Lorenz-63
systems, and reactive Burger’s equation in both periodic and chaotic regimes. This research
demonstrates that while all methods perform adequately in simpler nonlinear problems, their effectiveness diverges significantly in highly chaotic systems. Specifically, the Particle Filter method achieves the most accurate parameter estimates with the lowest error standard deviation in the challenging chaotic regime of reactive Burger’s equation, albeit requiring larger ensemble sizes to maintain diversity after resampling. These findings provide valuable insights for selecting
appropriate data assimilation methods in computational fluid dynamics applications, particularly for detonation phenomena and shock wave propagation where parameters must be inferred from limited observational data. This work contributes to the broader understanding of how different assimilation techniques perform under varying degrees of nonlinearity and chaotic behavior in reactive flow systems

title: Formally verified temporal logic validation
abstract: Mission-time Linear Temporal Logic (MLTL) is a finite, discrete, and interval-bounded version of the popular Linear Temporal Logic (LTL), frequently used to specify requirements for safety-critical systems such as aircraft and spacecraft. Despite its growing use in formal verification, MLTL suffers from a specification bottleneck, as system designers lack adequate means to validate that formal specifications match their intent. To address this, we develop verified theoretical foundations and user-friendly tooling for MLTL formula validation. We present the WEST algorithm, which transforms MLTL formulas into regular expressions that succinctly characterize the set of traces satisfying the given formula. We provide pencil and paper proofs of the correctness of the WEST algorithm, theoretical complexity analysis, and empirical evaluations of its performance. Furthermore, we formalize the WEST algorithm in the Isabelle/HOL theorem prover and prove its correctness. The WEST tool then efficiently implements the WEST algorithm via C++ bitset operations, and provides a user-friendly, interactive graphical user interface for MLTL formula validation. Lastly, we conduct a comprehensive cross validation of the WEST tool by comparing its output with other MLTL tools, including a code export from the Isabelle/HOL formalization of the WEST algorithm, imbuing the WEST tool with a high degree of trustworthiness. Collectively, these contributions significantly enhance the usability and reliabi

title: The bilingual cocktail party problem: Selective attention in speech-in-speech environments
abstract: Individuals face a constant stream of noise and speech distractors that compete for attention and cognitive resources during everyday tasks. This challenge is exacerbated for bilinguals, who navigate multiple linguistic systems. The present study investigated selective attention processes of English-Spanish bilinguals, specifically concerning auditory distractors. Two key factors hypothesized to predict dichotic listening performance are bilinguals’ familiarity with the distractor language (i.e., whether it is presented in their first or second language) and the match between target and distractor languages. Participants completed a dichotic listening task in which they listened to audiobook segments while being simultaneously exposed to distracting movie audios. Target and distractor languages were manipulated to include both English and Spanish conditions. Participants then responded to memory questions, as well as complete executive functions and language tasks. The results showed that participants performed better when the target stimuli were presented in their first language, and that having speech distractors of either language impeded performance compared to silent conditions. The interaction between target and distractor languages did not predict how well participants performed in the memory task. Additionally, I examined individual differences in executive functions and bilingualism as potential moderators but found no consistent or reliable patterns. Through these i

title: Statistical learning and inference for confidential data under the differential privacy framework
abstract:
With the advancement of personal technologies such as smartphones, the increasing availability of sensitive data in modern statistical and machine learning applications presents significant challenges for protecting individual privacy while maintaining statistical utility. This dissertation develops statistical methodologies for estimation and inference under the framework of differential privacy.

The first part of this work addresses the problem of false discovery rate (FDR) control in multiple hypothesis testing while preserving privacy. We propose DP-AdaPT, a differentially private procedure that controls the false discovery rate at a user-specified level $\alpha$. This method introduces a novel $p$-value transformation and a novel mirror peeling algorithm, ensuring privacy protection without sacrificing statistical accuracy. Empirical studies show that DP-AdaPT outperforms existing private methods by maintaining high accuracy and significantly reducing computation.

In the second part, we investigate the behavior of stochastic gradient descent (SGD) under randomized subsampling—a key component of differentially private SGD (DP-SGD). We study the asymptotic properties of DP-SGD and show that the asymptotic variance of the DP-SGD estimator consists of three components: statistical error, subsampling-induced variability, and privacy-induced noise. Building on the asymptotic distribution, we develop two inference methods, plug-in and random scaling, that yield valid confiden

title: Regulation of metabolic homeostasis in the heart, liver, and kidney in Drosophila melanogaster
abstract:
Lipids play a critical role in maintaining metabolic homeostasis, yet their organ-specific regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. Using Drosophila melanogaster as a robust genetic model, we investigate the diverse roles of lipid-mediated pathways in health and disease across distinct physiological systems, including cardiac protection, renal lipid homeostasis, and hepatic stress responses. In the first project, we studied the role of mTORC2 in protecting the heart from high-fat diet (HFD)-induced cardiomyopathy via mitochondrial fission in Drosophila. In the second project, we demonstrate that renal plasmalogen biosynthesis is essential for maintaining circulating plasmalogen levels in Drosophila. In the third project, we studied the role of phenylalanine-dependent FOXO regulation in starvation-induced hepatic steatosis in Drosophila Larval oenocytes. 
HFD induces cardiac dysfunction, accompanied by mitochondrial dysfunction, a key contributor to heart impairment under nutrient overload. Thus, maintaining mitochondrial health is crucial for protecting the heart during HFD stress. Mitochondrial fission, a key quality control process, has been implicated in protecting the heart. In this study, we demonstrate that mTORC2 promotes mitochondrial fission to protect the heart from HFD-induced cardiomyopathy in Drosophila. Heart-specific knockdown of rictor, a core component of mTORC2, inhibits HFD-induced mitochondrial fission and impairs cardiac contractile function. This

title: Prediction and monitoring with machine learning under complex dependencies for swine production data
abstract:
Machine learning has become an integral part of modern data analysis, yet the statistical reliability of these methods is often hindered by the complex nature of real-world data. Standard ML algorithms frequently assume data are independent and identically distributed, which is always violated in the case of hierarchical structures and serial correlations existing in data originating from swine production systems. This dissertation provides some innovative statistical machine learning frameworks that have been designed for solving such problems, focusing on reliable predictions with quantified uncertainty and robust process monitoring.

In Chapter 2, we develop a hierarchical split conformal prediction interval approach that integrates mixed-effects models into machine learning algorithms, leading to narrower and more informative prediction intervals by leveraging the subject-specific information. We show improved predictive performance compared to alternative methods. In Chapter 3, we introduce a Bayesian Neural Network with Random Effects (BNN-RE) to enable dynamic construction of ongoing prediction intervals that adapt to new data while accounting for the data hierarchy. We explore different update strategies, demonstrating improvements in predictive performance compared to standard BNNs across updates. In Chapter 4, we enhance Statistical Process Control (SPC) in a multi-process system with serial correlation. Building upon sequential de-correlation and distance-based sup

title: RIOCZ: Kernel-level ransomware detection and zone quarantine for ZNS SSDs
abstract: This paper introduces RIOCZ, a kernel-level ransomware defense framework for Zoned Namespace SSDs that monitors low-level I/O operations using heuristic analysis. Designed for Linux systems, RIOCZ intercepts I/O requests via the Device Mapper framework and classifies activity based on features such as file changes, deletions, and entropy variations. When ransomware-like behavior is detected, the system transitions affected zones to a novel quarantined state, ensuring data integrity and preventing further malicious modification. Two unlock methods are proposed: administrative command with a cryptographic key and hardware-based access, offering flexibility and robust security for enterprise environments.

title: Resilient roads for the future: Localized design, sustainable materials, and climate-adaptive pavement solutions
abstract:
This study explored three critical dimensions of pavement engineering aimed at improving the performance, durability, and sustainability of low-volume roads using scientific design methods, innovative material-stabilization techniques, and advanced modeling to understand, predict, and mitigate the detrimental effects of moisture on structural integrity of pavement under adverse climatic conditions. The overarching goal of this research was to deliver practical methodologies that inform cost-effective, environmentally sustainable, and technically sound solutions for road construction, maintenance, and rehabilitation activities, such as partial and full depth reclamation.
The first part of the study established a mix design for Otta seal surfacing of low-volume roads, emphasizing the inadequacy of guidelines derived from Norway’s Overby method when applied to local conditions in Iowa. By developing a modified McLeod method, this study accounted for local aggregate properties, binder types, and application rate variations. Laboratory investigations and field trials confirmed that the modified McLeod method reduced aggregate loss, dust generation, and roughness while significantly outperforming the Overby guidelines in terms of life-cycle cost and performance metrics. The mix design approach not only demonstrated economic efficiency but also promoted the use of recycled aggregates such as recycled concrete aggregate and slag, encouraging their integration into future Otta seal ap

title: The use of carcass traits as indicators of heifer pregnancy in Angus cattle
abstract:
A primary driver of profitability in the cow-calf sector of the beef cattle industry is the reproductive ability of females, as revenue generated through calf sales to offsets female input costs and contributes to net income. An important measure of reproductive performance is heifer pregnancy, or the ability of heifers to conceive within the first breeding season. Heifers that fail to become pregnant in the first breeding season are often seen as an economic loss and culled from the herd. While these females may be fed out and marketed as feedlot cattle, heifer development costs typically exceed the cost of developing feedlot cattle. The higher capital investment of breeding heifers makes it difficult to generate a positive return on investment when potential replacement heifers are marketed as fed cattle. 
Heifer pregnancy is influenced by both management and genetics, and research regarding both factors has been performed. Management practices have focused on developing heifers to an ideal body weight at breeding and using body condition scoring (BCS) to evaluate fat coverage. While BCS may provide a good estimate of fat coverage, it is subjective to the individual assigning scores and their expertise. Furthermore, body weight and BCS alone are insufficient for assessing true body composition.
Genetic methods of evaluating heifer pregnancy have been successful, but heritability estimates are low, indicating that genetic progress is made at a slow rate through selection. Un

title: The impact of haptic imagery within multisensory design for the hotel industry on Generation Z customer satisfaction
abstract:
Sensory reception plays a crucial role in shaping how individuals experience art and design, particularly within hotel interiors. Despite its significance, there is a notable research gap regarding how the senses can be strategically harnessed to enhance hotel environments and guest satisfaction. Integrating sight, smell, touch, sound, and taste offers the potential to elevate the guest experience, especially for Generation Z, who prioritize personalized and immersive environments.
This study examines the influence of sensory perception—with a focus on haptic imagery—on hotel design preferences and satisfaction among Generation Z guests. Employing a quantitative methodology, the research combines a literature review with online questionnaires. Participants from the target demographic assessed realistic renderings of hotel interiors, and their feedback was evaluated using a customized satisfaction scale.
Findings reveal that higher levels of sensory design are associated with increased guest satisfaction, particularly in lobbies, corridors, and dining areas. The data also highlight gender racial and ethnic differences: males expressed greater satisfaction with both low-sensory guest rooms and high-sensory dining areas, while White/Caucasian participants favored both low and high extremes of sensory design, and Asian participants preferred moderate sensory levels.
These results emphasize the value of tailoring sensory design strategies to specific demographic preferences to opt

title: Techno economic analysis and life cycle assessment of synthetic spider silk production in large scale
abstract:
Spider silk is a remarkable natural biomaterial renowned for its unparalleled combination of
tensile strength, elasticity, toughness, and biocompatibility, surpassing many synthetic polymers
like Kevlar and offering immense potential for diverse applications. These include
high-performance textiles, such as lightweight protective fabrics, and biomedical innovations, like
sutures, tissue scaffolds, and drug delivery systems. Despite its promise, the production of natural
spider silk faces significant hurdles that render large-scale harvesting impractical. Spiders’
territorial and cannibalistic behaviors prevent efficient farming, while their low silk yields and the
labor-intensive extraction process escalate costs. Additionally, ethical and ecological concerns
surrounding mass spider farming further limit its viability. Synthetic spider silk, produced
through recombinant DNA technology, emerges as a promising solution to overcome these barriers
by enabling scalable, controlled production that mimics the structural and functional properties
of natural silk. However, the economic feasibility and environmental sustainability of large-scale
synthetic spider silk manufacturing remain poorly understood, posing critical questions for its
commercialization. This thesis aims to address these knowledge gaps by conducting a
comprehensive techno-economic analysis (TEA) and life cycle assessment (LCA) of synthetic
spider silk production using Escherichia coli (E. coli) as the host organism

title: Three essays on online word-of-mouth and user behavior in online environments
abstract:
Online word-of-mouth (WOM) plays a vital role in shaping consumer behavior and firm performance in digital environments. While prior research has made substantial progress in understanding the influence of online reviews and textual content, important gaps remain regarding the role of visual content, emotional ambiguity, and manipulated expectations. This dissertation addresses these gaps through three essays that explore emerging psychological and behavioral mechanisms in online WOM using large-scale social media and review platform data.
The first essay examines how emotions conveyed through images affect user engagement on social media. By combining vision-language models with causal inference techniques, it reveals that certain discrete emotions, such as anger and surprise, significantly boost engagement, while joy has no discernible effect. The second essay introduces emotional ambiguity, uncertainty in emotional valence, as a novel factor influencing engagement. It shows that ambiguous content, which prompts deeper cognitive processing, can be more engaging, especially in influencer contexts. The third essay investigates how fake reviews distort consumer expectations, leading to non-linear satisfaction outcomes. It finds that consumers with higher cognitive engagement are more resilient to manipulated expectations.
Collectively, these essays advance the literature on online WOM by integrating affective computing, causal modeling, and drawing on psychological theories. T

title: Beyond the PIN: TrueYou – A context-aware mobile authentication system using one-class learning on behavioral and dynamic biometrics
abstract: Mobile authentication must balance security and usability, especially as traditional methods like PINs remain vulnerable to attacks such as brute-force attempts, shoulder surfing, and credential theft. This paper proposes a behavioral biometric authentication system that leverages keystroke dynamics and touch interaction patterns to enhance mobile security. The system captures key features including press intervals, hold durations, touch coordinates, hover patterns, back-press events, honeypot interactions, and location context. Developed using React Native and Expo, the application stores structured interaction data for model training and analysis. A sliding window approach is used to construct dynamic keystroke sequences, which are then used to train unsupervised one-class classification models: Isolation Forest, One-Class SVM, and an LSTM-based Autoencoder. These models are trained on legitimate user data to detect anomalous behavior indicative of imposter access. Experimental results show that the Autoencoder achieves the best overall performance, with high accuracy, precision, and recall. The findings demonstrate the viability of behavioral biometrics combined with one-class learning as a lightweight, continuous, and secure mobile authentication method.

title: Ghost dog: The role of dynamic frequency monitoring in application and anomaly detection on Intel microarchitectures
abstract: Given the wide purview of microarchitectural attacks, it is crucial to detect the ongoing attacks in systems, and the use of frequency scaling governors is an attractive solution, especially given its widespread implementation across Intel, AMD, and ARM processors. High performance is necessary to ensure the economics of cloud computing where resources are shared amongst multiple users, and the use of CPU cache while also maintaining the security of user data is vital. Further optimizations such as memory deduplication expose the computational resources to cache side channel attacks. Prior to Ghost Dog, detection mechanisms have been suboptimal for a number of reasons: (1) large performance impact, (2) low generality, (3) narrow scope, and (4) difficulty of automation. Ghost Dog leverages machine learning—namely Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Support Vector Machines (SVMs), Random Forest (RF), and Decision Tree (DT), with RF shining as the strongest candidate—to find patterns in Intel’s frequency scaling governor profile, thereby enabling the classification of applications and distinguishing anomalies. Due to its groundbreaking nature, Ghost Dog provides multiple paths for future research to extend its capability and use.

title: Topics in integrating image data into statistical analysis
abstract:
The integration of image data into statistical analysis has grown increasingly important with advances in high-resolution sensors and computer vision technologies. Unlike traditional tabular data, image data introduces unique challenges, including high dimensionality, spatial correlation, and missing values. This work investigates methods to enhance the statistical integration, interpretability, and reliability of image-based analyses.
The first project focuses on leveraging the abundance of satellite imagery as auxiliary information to improve land use prediction, particularly in settings with limited manually sampled data. We establish links between National Resources Inventory (NRI) sample points and geospatial information derived from satellite images by modeling the relationship between image-derived features and NRI data. To capture environmental heterogeneity across locations and underlying spatial structure, we propose a spatial clustering method—Fused Lasso Assisted hypothesis Testing (FLAT). FLAT assesses spatial similarity using a fused lasso framework constructed on a minimum spanning tree (MST). A key innovation of our method is an additional merging step designed to address the common issue of under-clustering in tree-based fused lasso approaches. We provide theoretical guarantees by proving the selection consistency of the FLAT method. title: Enhancing foam concrete sustainability with low-carbon cement, municipal solid waste, and artificial intelligent analysis
abstract: Utilizing solid waste and artificial intelligence (AI) has become more popular due to the growing sustainability demand. The research aimed to enhance FC sustainability and performance by addressing the need for solid waste and limitations in experimental data through synthetic data generation and AI-based predictive modeling. The content of this dissertation was structured into four distinct studies, each serving as an independent paper focusing on a particular facet of the overarching research objectives. The first part evaluated the use of MSWI-BA as sand in FC. The second part evaluated its usage as a partial substitute for river sand, with and without 30% limestone fines. In the first study, MSWI-BA underwent different pre-treatments, hydrated lime, hot water, and sodium hydroxide (NaOH) to improve MSWI-BA compatibility with the binder and mitigate irregular expansion. The second study used a different method to use MSWI-BA with and without 30% limestone fines. Experimental tests for both studies assessed fresh and hardened properties of FC, including flowability, fresh and dry densities, compressive strength, electrical resistivity, water absorption, and free drying shrinkage. Linear mixed-effects modeling was used for statistical analyses in the first study and Scheffé’s polynomial and nonlinear least squares models in the second. The Gaussian copula model was used in the third paper to generate a synthetic dataset for FC, preserving the statistical of real experimenta

title: Interfacial thermal transport of 1D nanoscale materials: Experiment and a unified model
abstract: Understanding heat transport across nanoscale interfaces is crucial for advancing fundamental science and engineering of next-generation electronic, photonic, and energy devices. Despite significant progress, fundamental aspects, including the interfacial transport mechanism, temperature dependence, and the non-equilibrium among energy carriers, remain active in research. This dissertation addresses some of these challenges through experimental methods and theoretical modeling. First, we experimentally investigate temperature-dependent interfacial thermal conductance using nano-resolved Raman thermometry. Our results validate the close relationship between interfacial thermal conductance and material heat capacities but point out discrepancies when describing interfacial transport solely from bulk material properties. To resolve this, the equivalent interfacial medium (EIM) model that departs from the conventional phonon reflection-transmission paradigm is introduced. Under the EIM, interfacial localized phonon modes whose properties are governed by a proposed characteristic temperature are argued to mediate thermal energy. We demonstrate that this interface characteristic temperature is distinct from the Debye temperature of the bulk materials that form the interface. The model demonstrates that the temperature-dependent interfacial thermal conductance is universal regardless of the interface type when normalized to the interface characteristic temperature, where literature

title: Advancing Influenza A virus monitoring in swine populations: sample types, detection strategies and molecular epidemiology
abstract:
Influenza A virus (IAV) is a significant respiratory pathogen in swine, with substantial implications for both animal and human health. This dissertation aims to address critical gaps in the understanding of IAV dynamics in swine populations, focusing on macroepidemiological trends, detection at the human-swine interface, and the optimization of sampling and diagnostic strategies for effective surveillance. Considering (a) the limited understanding of IAV detection in the US, (b) the animal and public health importance of IAV in swine, and (c) the need to explore improving sampling methods for IAV surveillance, this dissertation aims to explore the macroepidemiological aspects, human-swine interface and diagnostics strategies to enhance IAV monitoring in the U.S. swine industry. The overall objectives of this dissertation were: (a) to characterize macroepidemiological trends of IAV detection in swine populations over time, (b) to evaluate IAV dynamics at the human-swine interface, and (c) to optimize sampling and diagnostic strategies for IAV surveillance in swine populations.
Chapter 2 examined macroepidemiological trends of IAV detection in porcine samples submitted to veterinary diagnostic laboratories (VDLs) in the United States from 2004 to 2024. This study aimed to characterize the macroepidemiological aspects of IAV reverse transcription real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-rtPCR) and detection of IAV subtypes n by RT-rtPCR assays in samples submitted from January 2

title: Robust, optimal, safe, and stable visual-inertial based navigation of autonomous  vehicle with neural network in feedback loop
abstract:
As autonomous Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) gain widespread adoption across various domains, ensuring their safe and reliable operation in previously unseen environments becomes increasingly critical. Yet autonomous vehicle navigation in complex and dynamic settings remains challenging due to the presence of moving objects, uncertainties about environment and disturbances. This dissertation addresses these challenges by improving the robustness, safety, and stability of autonomous UAVs through advancements in both perception and control.
On the perception side, we propose a dynamic semantic Visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (VSLAM) method capable of identifying both known and unknown dynamic objects. The proposed approach integrates an unsupervised segmentation with object detection and optical flow to classify image regions as static or dynamic, based on semantic labels and pixel movements. Optical flow gradients are leveraged to mitigate the influence of camera motion, and a consistency check based on scene flow further refines the segmentation results, enabling robust pose and map estimation in dynamic environments. Experimental validation using benchmark datasets demonstrates improved localization and mapping performance over traditional and semantic VSLAM systems, particularly when unknown dynamic objects are present.

title: Intensive Care Unit Patient Outcome Prediction Using ν-Support Vector Classification and Stochastic Signal Processing–Based Feature Extraction Techniques: Algorithm Development and Validation Study
abstract:
Background:
Intensive care units (ICUs) treat patients with life-threatening illnesses. Worldwide, intensive care demand is massive. Predicting patient outcomes in ICUs holds significant importance for health care operation management. Nevertheless, it remains a challenging problem that researchers and health care practitioners have yet to overcome. While the newly emerging health digital trace data offer new possibilities, such data contain complex time series and patterns. Although researchers have devised severity score systems, traditional machine learning models with feature engineering, and deep learning models that use raw clinical data to predict ICU outcomes, existing methods have limitations.

Objective:
This study aimed to develop a novel feature extraction and machine learning framework to repurpose and extract features with strong predictive power from patients’ health digital traces for ICU outcome prediction.

Methods:
Guided by signal processing techniques and medical domain knowledge, the proposed framework introduces a novel, signal processing–based feature engineering method to extract highly predictive features from ICU digital trace data. We rigorously evaluated this method on a real-world ICU dataset, demonstrating significant improvements over both traditional and deep learning baseline methods. The method was then evaluated using a real-world database to assess prediction accuracy and feature representativeness.

title: A Real-Time Signal-Based Wavelet Long Short-Term Memory Method for Length-of-Stay Prediction for the Intensive Care Unit: Development and Evaluation Study
abstract:
Background:
Efficient allocation of health care resources is essential for long-term hospital operation. Effective intensive care unit (ICU) management is essential for alleviating the financial strain on health care systems. Accurate prediction of length-of-stay in ICUs is vital for optimizing capacity planning and resource allocation, with the challenge of achieving early, real-time predictions.

Objective:
This study aimed to develop a predictive model, namely wavelet long short-term memory model (WT-LSTM), for ICU length-of-stay using only real-time vital sign data. The model is designed for urgent care settings where demographic and historical patient data or laboratory results may be unavailable; the model leverages real-time inputs to deliver early and accurate ICU length-of-stay predictions.

Methods:
The proposed model integrates discrete wavelet transformation and long short-term memory (LSTM) neural networks to filter noise from patients’ vital sign series and improve length-of-stay prediction accuracy. Model performance was evaluated using the electronic ICU database, focusing on 10 common ICU admission diagnoses in the database.

Results:
The results demonstrate that WT-LSTM consistently outperforms baseline models, including linear regression, LSTM, and bidirectional long short-term memory, in predicting ICU length-of-stay using vital sign data, achieving significant improvements in mean square error. title: Soybean maturity prediction using two-dimensional contour plots from drone-based time series imagery
abstract: Plant breeding programs require assessment and understanding of days to maturity for accurate selection and placement of entries in appropriate tests. Soybean [Glycine max (L.) Merr.] breeding programs, in the early stages of the breeding pipeline, assign relative maturity ratings to experimental varieties that indicate their suitable maturity zones. Traditionally, the estimation of maturity rating value has involved breeders manually inspecting fields and assessing maturity value visually. This approach relies heavily on expert judgment, making it subjective and demanding considerable time and effort. This study aimed to develop a machine learning (ML) model for evaluating soybean maturity using uncrewed aerial system (UAS)–based time series imagery. Images were captured at 3-day intervals, beginning as the earliest varieties started maturing and continuing until the last varieties fully matured. The data collected for this experiment consisted of 22,043 plots collected across 3 years and represent relative maturity groups 1.6–3.9. We utilized contour plot images extracted from the time series UAS imagery as input for a neural network model. This contour plot approach encoded the temporal and spatial variation within each plot into a single image. A deep learning model was trained to utilize this contour plot to predict maturity ratings. This model demonstrates a significant improvement in accuracy and robustness, achieving up to 85% accuracy. The predictive model offers a s

title: End‐to‐end instance segmentation framework for automated pavement distress assessment using unmanned aerial vehicle‐derived digital orthophoto maps
abstract: This study presents a novel framework for automated detection and segmentation of pavement distresses using high-resolution digital orthophoto maps captured by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). While recent UAV-based research often relies on manual measurements from rasterized digital models, only a few studies have employed automated methods for analyzing pavement distress, primarily using raw aerial image tiles. Developing a distress detection system specifically suited for UAV-based, scale-variant orthomaps is complex but offers significant advantages. This study developed a comprehensive dataset from UAV-derived orthophotos and utilized geographic information system tools to create precise vector annotations of various pavement distress types. These annotations were transformed into standard object detection formats to train state-of-the-art computer vision models. The study evaluated both one-stage (YOLOv7, YOLOv8 with YOLACT [You Only Look At CoefficienTs] segmentation head) and two-stage (Mask R-CNN) instance segmentation networks under various configurations. The YOLOv7 model with low hyperparameter settings achieved the highest performance, attaining mean average precision scores of 0.70 for box detection and 0.67 for mask segmentation. Inferencing strategies, such as strided inference with different tile sizes, were employed to optimize detection across varying scales. The detection results from the YOLOv7 model demonstrated a satisfactory agreement with manual measu

title: Salt Circle
abstract:
Salt Circle is a book of poems structured by the logics of the sestina. The sestina is, as defined by The Poetry Foundation, “a complex French verse form, usually unrhymed, consisting of six stanzas of six lines each and a three-line envoi. The end words of the first stanza are repeated in a different order as end words in each of the subsequent five stanzas; the closing envoi contains all six words, two per line, placed in the middle and at the end of the three lines.” The book includes several sestinas, as well as haiku sequences, sonnets, prose poems, and free verse poems. It also follows the form on a larger scale; it contains seven sections (six “stanzas” and an “envoi”) and an introductory sestina and a closing septina, an evolution of the form constructed specifically for this project. 

The through-line of the text explores how humans both make and refuse meaning in their lives. It is about how we interact with the world around us, how the world interacts with us, how our survival is dependent on interconnectedness, how fragile an ecosystem is our sense of personhood. It’s about language’s paradoxical capacity and failure to accurately document experiences of love and grief, of cognition and embodiment. Borrowing tools of inquiry from neuro- and psycholinguistics, evolutionary biology, and mathematics, Salt Circle cries while it plays, laughs while in mourning, makes poems out of equations, questions everything, and acquiesces to the absence of answers.

title: Conversational LLM-Based Decision Support for Defect Classification in AFM Images
abstract: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) has emerged as a powerful tool for nanoscale imaging and quantitative characterization of organic (e.g., live cells, proteins, DNA, and lipid bilayers) and inorganic (e.g., silicon wafers and polymers) specimens. However, image artifacts in AFM height and peak force error images directly affect the precision of nanomechanical measurements. Experimentalists face considerable challenges in obtaining high-quality AFM images due to the requirement of specialized expertise and constant manual monitoring. Another challenge is the lack of high-quality AFM datasets to train machine learning models for automated defect detection. In this work, we propose a two-step AI framework that combines a vision-based deep learning (DL) model for classifying AFM image defects with a large language model (LLM)-based conversational assistant that provides real-time corrective guidance in natural language, making it particularly valuable for non-AFM experts aiming to obtain high-quality images. We curated an annotated AFM defect dataset spanning organic and inorganic samples to train the defect detection model. Our defect classification model achieves 91.43% overall accuracy, with a recall of 93% for tip contamination and 60% not-tracking defects. We further develop an intuitive user interface that enables seamless interaction with the DL model and integrates an LLM-based guidance feature to support users in understanding defects and improving future experiments. title: Multi-Modal Sensor Fusion for Proactive Blockage Prediction in mmWave Vehicular Networks
abstract: Vehicular communication systems operating in the millimeter wave (mmWave) band are highly susceptible to signal blockage from dynamic obstacles such as vehicles, pedestrians, and infrastructure. To address this challenge, we propose a proactive blockage prediction framework that utilizes multi-modal sensing, including camera, GPS, LiDAR, and radar inputs in an infrastructure-to-vehicle (I2V) setting. This approach uses modality-specific deep learning models to process each sensor stream independently and fuses their outputs using a softmax-weighted ensemble strategy based on validation performance. Our evaluations, for up to 1.5s in advance, show that the camera-only model achieves the best standalone trade-off with an F1-score of 97.1% and an inference time of 89.8ms. A camera+radar configuration further improves accuracy to 97.2% F1 at 95.7ms. Our results display the effectiveness and efficiency of multi-modal sensing for mmWave blockage prediction and provide a pathway for proactive wireless communication in dynamic environments.

title: ANALYSIS OF THE FRIENDS TV SERIES USING  NLP AND MACHINE LEARNING
abstract: This project presents a comprehensive analysis of the Friends TV series using advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML) techniques. It employs transformer-based models to perform automated theme classification, character interaction network analysis, and sentiment exploration on subtitle and transcript data. Additionally, the project features a content-based recommendation engine and an interactive user interface built with Gradio, making complex analyses accessible to non-technical users. A conversational AI agent developed via the n8n platform enhances user engagement by providing dynamic, context-aware interactions related to the series. This work demonstrates the power of computational linguistics in media analytics and offers novel insights into one of the most popular sitcoms in television history.

title: The Role of Data Analytics in Ensuring  Clean and Safe Food Supply Chains
abstract:
The role of data analytics in ensuring clean and safe food supply chains has become a critical component in addressing food safety challenges in the modern, globalized food industry. As foodborne illnesses, contamination risks, and supply chain inefficiencies continue to affect consumer health and trust, data-driven solutions such as predictive analytics, blockchain technology, and real-time monitoring have emerged as transformative tools (IBM, n.d.; World Health Organization [WHO], n.d.). This literature review explores the contributions of data analytics to food safety management, highlighting predictive models for contamination detection, blockchain for enhanced traceability, and IoT for real-time monitoring. Case studies from Walmart, IBM, and Nestlé demonstrate the impact of these technologies, reducing food recall times and improving transparency. Despite the benefits, challenges such as data integration, cost barriers for SMEs, and regulatory gaps remain, necessitating further research into AI-driven automation and cost-effective blockchain solutions. 

Furthermore, the review examines key challenges including data quality, system interoperability, and resource constraints that hinder the adoption of these technologies. It also explores emerging solutions, such as AI-driven automation and cost-effective blockchain models, to enhance food safety across global supply chains. It also examines practical applications and case studies from industry leaders like Walmart and I

title: AI/ML-Powered Phishing Email Detection System: A Web App & Chrome Extension Approach
abstract:
Phishing attacks continue to be one of the most prevalent and successful cybersecurity threats, exploiting human psychology rather than technical vulnerabilities. Traditional email security solutions often fail to detect sophisticated phishing attempts that employ advanced social engineering techniques and mimic legitimate communications with high fidelity. This creative component presents the development of an AI-powered phishing email detection system that combines multiple detection approaches: machine learning classification trained on extensive datasets, artificial intelligence analysis using OpenAI's GPT models, and comprehensive security verification including WHOIS and DNS analysis.

The system consists of two main components designed to address different user needs and deployment scenarios. The first component is a comprehensive web application built with Flask that provides detailed email analysis capabilities for security professionals, IT administrators, and users requiring in-depth threat assessment. The second component is a Chrome browser extension that offers seamless, real-time protection for Gmail users, automatically scanning emails and displaying visual safety indicators without disrupting normal workflow.

The web application employs a multi-layered detection approach, utilizing a custom-trained Random Forest classifier with TF-IDF vectorization, GPT-powered semantic analysis for contextual understanding, and traditional security verification methods. The

title: How Can Games Transform Cities? Geogames as Tools for Research, Education, and Urban Praxis
abstract: Geogames have matured from an emergent field in the 2000s into a transformative intersection of game design, geographic information science, and games with a purpose. This thematic issue advances the geogames research, education, and praxis agenda through 10 articles organized into two sections. Section 1 establishes geogames as rigorous research and educational instruments, exploring their theoretical foundations, methodological applications, and pedagogical value for fostering spatial literacy and emotional engagement. Section 2 demonstrates geogames as operational tools for real‐world urban planning, showcasing their implementation in participatory consultations, communicative planning, and sustainability initiatives. These contributions frame geogames as a socio‐technical epistemology rather than mere representational or engagement tools, revealing their capacity to address complex contemporary urban challenges. By bridging virtual simulation with material intervention in games, this issue presents a unified framework for reimagining research, teaching, and the transformation of urban spaces through geogames—where the concept of Gaia (Earth as a living system) converges with gameplay—in an era marked by unprecedented spatial, environmental, and social challenges.

title: Peromyscus spp. Deer Mice as Rodent Model of Acute Leptospirosis
abstract: Leptospirosis is a global zoonotic disease affecting humans, wildlife, companion, and domestic animals. Incidental hosts can contract the disease directly or indirectly from asymptomatic reservoir hosts, most commonly small rodents. The Golden Syrian hamster is recognized as the dominant rodent model for acute leptospirosis because the animals are susceptible to many serovars and are used to maintain laboratory strains and test bacterin vaccine efficacy. However, hamsters are primarily used in survival-based studies, and investigations into host immune response and disease pathogenesis are limited. We found that Peromyscus leucopus white-footed deer mice are susceptible to acute leptospirosis, and thus might be an alternative rodent model. Furthermore, similar to hamsters, deer mice produce circulating foamy macrophages in response to Leptospira challenge. Deer mice exhibit differences in response to different serovars, clinical disease severity, kidney and liver lesions, and an overall sex effect, with male mice demonstrating more severe clinical signs and higher bacterial burden.

title: Guilty Pleas: History, Research, and Current Directions
abstract: Over the past four decades, guilty pleas have become increasingly prevalent globally (Fair Trials, 2017). Within the United States legal system, recent estimates suggest that over 95% of all criminal convictions – and in some jurisdictions, all convictions – are plea dispositions (Johnson, 2023; Wilford & Bornstein, 2023). Although the practice takes on different forms and labels (e.g., resolution discussions, cooperation agreements, abbreviated trials), guilty pleas decide most cases in many other jurisdictions as well, including Australia, Canada, England and Wales, Estonia, Georgia, Russia, and Scotland, among others (Brook et al., 2015; Fair Trials, 2017). While plea rates among adults can be suggestive of a general trend, it is difficult to estimate how these rates compare to those of juvenile defendants. The U.S. National Center for State Courts (2023) indicates that from 2017 to 2021, only 6.5%-12.3% of juvenile delinquency cases in 13 jurisdictions proceeded to a bench trial. In England and Wales in 2019, 46.9% of youth charged in juvenile (Youth) courts pleaded guilty at first appearance, and 58.4% of those charged in Crown Court eventually pleaded guilty (Evidence Based Justice Lab 2021). Thus, it appears that juvenile delinquency cases also reach plea dispositions frequently, though the rates might be lower than those of adults.

title: Probabilistic Method to Fuse Artificial Intelligence-Generated Underground Utility Mapping
abstract: Utility as-built plans, which typically provide information about underground utilities’ position and spatial locations, are known to comprise inaccuracies. Over the years, the reliance on utility investigations using an array of sensing equipment has increased in an attempt to resolve utility as-built inaccuracies and mitigate the high rate of accidental underground utility strikes during excavation activities. Adapting data fusion into utility engineering and investigation practices has been shown to be effective in generating information with improved accuracy. However, the complexities in data interpretation and associated prohibitive costs, especially for large-scale projects, are limiting factors. This paper addresses the problem of data interpretation, costs, and large-scale utility mapping with a novel framework that generates probabilistic inferences by fusing data from an automatically generated initial map with as-built data. The probabilistic inferences expose regions of high uncertainty, highlighting them as prime targets for further investigations. The proposed model is a collection of three main processes. First, the automatic initial map creation is a novel contribution supporting rapid utility mapping by subjecting identified utility appurtenances to utility inference rules. The second and third processes encompass the fusion of the created initial utility map with available knowledge from utility as-builts or historical satellite imagery data and then evalua

title: Interspecific allometry of sexual shape dimorphism in small-bodied and large-bodied geckos
abstract: At macroevolutionary scales across species, sexual dimorphism often covaries with body size, generating allometric trends. Such patterns are most evident for body size dimorphism, while trends in sexual shape dimorphism remain underexamined. Additionally, how small body sizes (miniaturization) affects such patterns is largely unknown. We evaluated allometry in sexual shape dimorphism in two families of geckos to determine whether changes in body size associate with changes in shape dimorphism. Using surface scans of head shape from nearly 600 individuals across 99 species, we found considerable variation in levels of sexual shape dimorphism across taxa, with some species displaying little dimorphism and others exhibiting large sexual differentiation. Interspecific trends differed between the two families, with strong negative allometry in Sphaeorodactylidae (a family with many small-bodied species), while Phyllodactylidae (a family containing few small-bodied species) displayed isometry and no discernible trend. Notably, greater sexual shape dimorphism was displayed in small-bodied sphaerodactylid species, and corresponded with females exhibiting more robust heads; consistent with sex-specific foraging strategies and dietary differences observed in this group. Our study reveals that interspecific allometry in traits other than body size can have a pervasive influence on patterns of phenotypic diversity across the tree of life.

title: The Use of Different Technologies to Provide a Virtual Grocery Store Tour for Nutrition Education
abstract: Dietitian-led grocery store tours (GSTs) educate consumers about nutrition. Virtual GSTs could increase access to nutrition education. A feasibility study was conducted to determine participant acceptability and their physiological responses to a virtual GST using immersive virtual reality (IVR), a desktop monitor (PC), or a tablet. Participants were asked to report to the laboratory on three occasions to view a virtual GST. Physiological measurements were collected, and participants completed questionnaires about their feelings of presence, nausea, mood, and enjoyment during the virtual GST. Participants experienced a greater sense of presence (IVR = 5.8, PC = 2.6, tablet = 2.6; p < 0.05) with a greater feeling of nausea (IVR = 1.7, PC = 0.4, tablet = 0.4; p < 0.05) in the IVR treatment. Participants enjoyed the IVR GST more than the tablet GST (IVR = 5.3, PC = 4.6, tablet = 4.1; p < 0.05). There were marginal effects of treatment on heart rate (p < 0.05) but not on other physiological measures. There were no differences in the participants’ willingness to recommend a virtual GST given the use of different technologies to a friend or in the participants’ reported mood. Virtual GSTs, using different technologies, may be a feasible approach to provide nutrition education.

title: Modeling nitrogen fluxes in a tile-drained cropping system in the Midwest using an enhanced SWAT model
abstract: Artificial (tile) drainage systems are extensively implemented across the U.S. Midwest to enhance crop production in poorly drained soils; however, they also pose environmental challenges by significantly altering nitrogen fluxes within agricultural landscapes. In response, sustainable intensification strategies seek to increase agricultural productivity while reducing environmental impacts, often through improved management practices such as cover cropping and conservation tillage. Effectively evaluating the trade-offs and synergies of agricultural management practices demands advanced modeling tools capable of representing coupled biogeochemical and hydrological processes across diverse spatial and temporal scales. This study presents the first application of an enhanced version of the Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT), integrated with Century/DayCent-based biogeochemical modules, to simulate both nitrate (NO3⁻) loss and nitrous oxide (N2O) fluxes in a tile-drained corn-soybean system. The model was applied to long-term field data (2004–2010) from an Iowa site with two treatments: with and without winter rye cover crops. With careful calibration, the model reproduced tile discharge and crop yields well and captured the direction and magnitude of cover-crop reductions in NO3⁻ losses. However, interannual variability in NO3⁻ export and event-scale N2O peaks remained difficult to reproduce, likely due to limited sampling frequency and structural constraints in soil hydrolo

title: A case analysis of strategic planning models in Assemblies of God churches
abstract: Understanding the use of strategic planning models is critical to the development of church growth. If churches are to continue to grow in the future, then planning is necessary to direct the church in the direction it wishes to go. The Bible mentions in Proverbs 29:18a "Where there is no vision the people perish" [King James Version]. A strategic planning model puts the people's vision into a tangible, easy to implement plan ready for action. It is absolutely imperative that churches develop a strategic planning model, no matter what the size or faith, if it wishes to accomplish its purpose. The same strategic planning model will not work for every church. Each church is different and has different needs and goals. Thus different methods will work for different churches. An examination of the methods that have worked will be necessary if a strategic model is to be created for the needs of small Assemblies of God churches.

title: Journalism students' attitudes on global understanding and intercultural experience
abstract: The factors of concern in this study are U.S. journalism students' possible misconceptions, lack of awareness, or lack of interest on global issues and foreign people. Several reasons can contribute to these factors: a low level of exposure to information concerning global issues, a low level of contact with people from cultures different from their own, and a low level of incentive toward knowledge and understanding of global issues at school and at home. This thesis attempts to be a case study of a group of ISU students attending classes in the Journalism and Mass Communication department. The focus of this study is on attitudes toward global understanding. Thomas S. Barrows, Stephen F. Klein, and John L. D. Clark (1981), in their book What College Students Know and Belief About Their World, explain that global understanding implies "being aware of nations beyond one's borders and of the issues that involve those nations and one's own" ( p. 7). The survey will serve as a needsassessment instrument. Depending on the results, workshops will be suggested in order to address possible problems.

title: Affirmative Action in India with Hierarchical Reservations
abstract:
India implements the world’s most complex affirmative action program through vertical and horizontal reservations. Although applicants can belong to at most one vertical category, they can qualify for multiple horizontal reservation categories simultaneously. We examine resource allocation problems in India, where horizontal reservations follow a hierarchical structure within a one-to-all horizontal matching framework. We introduce the hierarchical choice rule and show that it selects the most meritorious set of applicants. We thoroughly analyze the
properties of the aggregate choice rule, which comprises hierarchical choice rules across all vertical categories. We show that the generalized deferred acceptance mechanism, when coupled with this aggregate choice rule, is the unique stable and strategy-proof mechanism that eliminates justified envy.

title: Enhancing Student Teacher Supervision Through Hybridization: Adding e-Supervision to the Mix
abstract: Student teaching is a critical component of the preservice teacher preparation program which has a major role in preparing novices to teach. This capstone experience has been frequently examined and the subject of numerous reform measures. Clinical experiences for preservice teachers have recently seen new recommendations for increased supervisor observational visits to meet accreditation standards. In this study, we sought to determine Iowa State University student teachers’ perceptions of a hybridized supervision approach which included an electronic supervision component. Student teachers participated in one of two focus group sessions held during the final on-campus student teacher professional development session. A researcher not involved with the supervision or grading of the student teachers facilitated the interviews. Interviews were later transcribed and analyzed. Three major themes emerged: Benefits to Student Teachers, Improving the e-Supervision Process, and Benefits to the Teacher Education Program. We conclude that e-supervision has the potential to improve the quality of the student teacher experience and the teacher education program. Recommendations for implementation and further research are provided.

title: Preservice teacher cluster memberships in an edtech course: A study of their TPACK development
abstract: Researchers have been examining preservice teachers’ development of TPACK in edtech courses for years. However, most empirical studies used small samples to look at preservice teachers’ TPACK development in the edtech courses. With a small dataset, it is hard to know whether there consistently exist knowledge gaps in preservice teachers’ prior knowledge and TPACK development in the edtech course. Studies with large samples are needed because they provide a large amount of empirical data that can be used as strong evidence for justifying whether the edtech course has any impact on preservice teachers’ TPACK development across all demographic and prior knowledge groups. Thus, the purpose of this study was to examine eighteen cohorts of preservice teachers’ pre-TPACK scores and their cluster assignment, as well as their post-TPACK scores in a required edtech course. A two-step cluster analysis was used based on pre-TPACK scores and demographics to identify groups of preservice teachers that share common characteristics in their pre-TPACK scores. A two-cluster model was a good fit (cluster 1 - lower pre-TPACK scores and cluster 2 - higher pre-TPACK scores). Independent-sample t-tests were run to test whether there were differences in the post-TPACK scores. Findings revealed that cluster 2 preservice teachers had higher post-TPACK scores. These results might help teacher educators make data-driven decisions to design targeted instructions for diverse preservice teacher groups. Det

title: Habitat amount and edge effects, not perch proximity, nest exposure, or vegetation diversity affect cowbird parasitism in agricultural landscapes
abstract:
Context
Prior research documented relationships between brown-headed cowbird (Molothrus ater) brood parasitism and edge effects, proximity of perches, and nest exposure. Those relationships have not been evaluated in agroecosystems containing extremes of fragmentation and vegetation diversity.

Objectives
We compared three existing hypoth-eses on how cowbirds locate host nests with two new hypotheses regarding habitat amount and vegetation diversity to determine how the configuration and location of agricultural conservation practices affect grassland bird nest parasitism rates and predicted rates for eight common conservation practices.

Methods
We assessed cowbird parasitism of grass-land bird nests on corn and soybean farms in Iowa, USA, and measured perch proximity, nest exposure, edge effects, habitat amount, and vegetation diver-sity for each nest. We fit a global generalized linear mixed-effects model and compared importance of model parameters using odds ratios. We predicted parasitism likelihood for every subset model and averaged predictions to explore individual effects.

Results
The variables that most influenced para-sitism rates included main effects for nest initiation day-of-season (OR = 0.71, CI₉₅ = 0.60–0.84) and the landscape variables of distance to nearest crop edge (0.63, 0.51–0.76) and proportion of grass land cover within 660 m (0.75, 0.57–1.00). We found little sup-port that perch proximity, nest exposure, or n

title: Laboratory and field ovipositional behavior of European corn borer, Ostrinia nubilalis (Hübner), females in the presence of neem, a natural botanical, and an emulsifier
abstract: Application of neem concentrations, 2,500, 5,000, and 10,000 ppm azadirachtin, on glass plates reduced the number of European corn borer, Ostrinia nubilalis (Hubner), egg masses oviposited in the laboratory. The emulsifier, Triton X-100, neither reduced nor inhibited oviposition. In a no-choice test conducted in the field during 1994, oviposition was reduced, but not inhibited by Triton X-100 or neem concentrations plus Triton X-100. Nearly three times as many egg ·masses were laid on plants sprayed with water as on plants sprayed with Triton X-100, and nearly four times as many egg masses were laid on plants sprayed with water as on plants sprayed with neem plus Triton X-100. In a choice test also conducted in the field during 1994, European corn borer females could distinguish between corn plants sprayed with water and plants sprayed with a neem concentration. European corn borer females preferred to oviposit on corn plants sprayed with water, rather than corn plants sprayed with neem concentrations plus Triton X-100. The number of egg masses oviposited on corn receiving water was not significantly different from the number of egg masses oviposited on corn receiving Triton X-100, suggesting that the reduction of egg mass numbers on corn receiving neem plus Triton X-100 was from the application ofneem.

title: Individual Family Service Plans: Do they reflect family-centered practice?
abstract: The Individual Family Service Plan (IFSP) has been described as the cornerstone of Part H (Deal, Dunst, & Trivette, 1989) and is both a process and a product (DeGangi, Royeen, & Wietlisbach, 1992). To date, the process for the development of the IFSP has been emphasized in both training of personnel and in research efforts. The purpose of this study is to examine the product, the IFSP document, to determine if it reflects the family-centered spirit of IDEA.

abstract: This study focuses on identification of possible crime locations and improvements of urban physical environment to reduce crime rates. Francis Gerard Stoks' Urban Public Space Model prepared especially for rape, guided this thesis. title: Interpreting FMS and SSQ Cybersickness Ratings via User Tolerance in Virtual Reality.
abstract: Cybersickness remains a persistent challenge limiting the usability of virtual reality (VR), yet commonly used subjective measures such as the Simulator Sickness Questionnaire (SSQ) and the Fast Motion Sickness (FMS) scale are often difficult to interpret in terms of user outcomes. In particular, there is limited guidance on how specific values on these scales relate to user tolerance or the likelihood that users will discontinue a VR experience due to discomfort. This work addresses this gap by calibrating cybersickness severity interpretations against early termination of a VR experience. In Study 1 (N = 183), participants played an immersive VR game for up to 20 minutes and were free to terminate the experience at any time. Using a Behavioral Risk Banding (BRB) framework, logistic regression linked a modified 0-10 version of the FMS (FMS-10) and post-exposure SSQ scores to dropout probability, yielding behaviorally grounded risk severity bands (mild, moderate, severe, extreme). Survival analyses then showed how these bands mapped onto tolerance over time, revealing a transitional region marked by heightened individual variability. Study 2 (N = 304) evaluated the robustness of these categories across variation in VR content and mitigation context by applying the Study 1 thresholds without re-estimation. Although absolute dropout risk varied, the ordering and behavioral meaning of severity categories were preserved. Together, these results provide a practical, behaviorally g

title: An Entrepreneurial Approach to International Engineering Programs
abstract: When John Grandin launched the International Engineering Program (IEP) at the University of Rhode Island (URI) in 1987, curricula and centers for entrepreneurship were considered the primary domain of colleges of business and were rarely associated with engineering, let alone international engineering programs. In fact, the IEP emerged as the first international engineering program that formalized a dual degree option with a department of languages and literatures in a college of arts and sciences and required an international internship experience in a language other than English. In many respects, the success of the IEP at URI and similar programs at other universities not only reflects the increasing importance of international initiatives in engineering and STEM, but also the significance of an entrepreneurial mindset in developing international programs and collaborations with industry.

title: GMesh: A Flexible Voronoi-Based Mesh Generator with Local Refinement for Watershed Hydrological Modeling
abstract: Partial Differential Equation (PDE)-based hydrologic models demand extensive preprocessing, creating a bottleneck and slowing down the model setup process. Mesh generation typically lacks integration with hydrological features like river networks. We present GHOST Mesh (GMesh), an automated, watershed-oriented mesh generator built within the Watershed Modeling Framework (WMF), to address this. While primarily designed for the GHOST hydrological model, GMesh’s functionalities can be adapted for other models. GMesh enables rapid mesh generation in Python by incorporating Digital Elevation Models (DEMs), flow direction maps, network topology, and online services. The software creates Voronoi polygons that maintain connectivity between river segments and surrounding hillslopes, ensuring accurate surface–subsurface interaction representation. Key features include customizable mesh generation and variable refinement to target specific watershed areas. We applied GMesh to Iowa’s Bear Creek watershed, generating meshes from 10,000 to 30,000 elements and analyzing their effects on simulated stream flows. Results show that higher mesh resolutions enhance peak flow predictions and reduce response time discrepancies, while local refinements improve model performance with minimal additional computation. GMesh’s open-source nature streamlines mesh generation, offering researchers an efficient solution for hydrological analysis and model configuration testing.

title: The Effect of Interlayer Delay on the Heat Accumulation, Microstructures, and Properties in Laser Hot Wire Directed Energy Deposition of Ti-6Al-4V Single-Wall
abstract: Laser hot wire directed energy deposition (LHW-DED) is a layer-by-layer additive manufacturing technique that permits the fabrication of large-scale Ti-6Al-4V (Ti64) components with a high deposition rate and has gained traction in the aerospace sector in recent years. However, one of the major challenges in LHW-DED Ti64 is heat accumulation, which affects the part quality, microstructure, and properties of as-built specimens. These issues require a comprehensive understanding of the layerwise heat-accumulation-driven process–structure–property relationship in as-deposited samples. In this study, a systematic investigation was performed by fabricating three Ti-6Al-4V single-wall specimens with distinct interlayer delays, i.e., 0, 120, and 300 s. The real-time acquisition of high-fidelity thermal data and high-resolution melt pool images were utilized to demonstrate a direct correlation between layerwise heat accumulation and melt pool dimensions. The results revealed that the maximum heat buildup temperature of the topmost layer decreased from 660 °C to 263 °C with an increase to a 300 s interlayer delay, allowing for better control of the melt pool dimensions, which then resulted in improved part accuracy. Furthermore, the investigation of the location-specific composition, microstructure, and mechanical properties demonstrated that heat buildup resulted in the coarsening of microstructures and, consequently, the reduction of micro-hardness with increasing height. title: Retention and Transfer of Procedural Tasks in Auto-Body Repair: An Instructional Design Study
abstract: This study examines how auto-body repair technicians retain and transfer procedural knowledge when performing complex tasks on electric vehicles. Focusing on the removal of auto-body glass, the project investigates challenges technicians face in recalling and executing multi-step procedures learned through virtual and instructor-led training. Participants are recruited from Bay Area auto-body shops and online technician communities, representing a workforce that operates in fast-paced, hands-on environments. Using an interpretive framework, the research explores gaps between training content and real-world performance, particularly where existing instructional formats may not fully support procedural accuracy. Guided by Bloom’s taxonomy and cognitive learning theory, the project proposes a multi-modal instructional solution that combines e-learning content with an interactive VR simulation developed in Unity. The prototype recreates the glass-removal workflow, leveraging immersive interaction mechanics and usability heuristics to reduce extrinsic cognitive load and strengthen skill transfer. The study aims to generate insights and design recommendations that enhance the effectiveness of procedural training for auto-body repair technicians.
